Remark 8.42 (What the test checks).

The three ingredients of Corollary [8.41](#b-01626) are computed independently: $Q_1$ and $S_1$ from the defect graphs of the equivariant quantum differential, $\mathrm{Gram}_{\rm 1}$ from the two-point graphs of Definition [8.37](#b-01606), and the conjugation from the exact reflection $\Theta_n$ transported by Proposition [8.34](#b-01589). Agreement tests the equivariant quantum master equation, the reflection compatibility of the scheme and the definition of $K_1$ together; the relation for $D_1$ states that the one-loop dilatation is self-adjoint for the tree inner product on each space of fixed classical weight, where $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ is a multiple of the identity.
8.10 Beyond one loop
Remark 8.43 (The definitions at higher order).

Every definition of this chapter is stated at all orders in $\hbar$: the counterterms are the singular parts graph by graph, with the functions $\varepsilon^{-m}\log^k\varepsilon$, $(m,k)\neq(0,0)$, and the counterterms of lower order inserted [C07, Thm B]; the obstruction at order $\hbar^{k}$ is a local $s$-cocycle once the lower orders are solved; $L=s+\hbar L_1+\hbar^2L_2+\cdots$ with $L\circ L=0$; the twisted differential is $r_\xi(\Lambda)$; the scheme acts by conjugation; the inner products and the adjointness are formal series. At two loops the graphs contain one-loop subgraphs with their counterterm vertices, and the defect graphs contain one special edge and one further cycle; the enumeration of graphs and the exact evaluation of their Schwinger integrals are algorithmic tasks of a size that grows with the loop order.
9. The cubic obstruction and the dilatation cochain at one loop

Chapter 4 removed the part of the one-loop obstruction with two legs by the finite counterterm $\tfrac{27}{16}$ units times $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V)$, and Chapter 6 read the dilatation coefficients off the scaling of the regulator. This chapter computes the part of the obstruction with three legs and solves the equation for the cubic finite counterterm, and then evaluates the equivariant structure of Chapter 8 along the dilatation: the arity-one counterterm, obstruction and finite counterterm along $\Delta$, the component $D_1$ of Definition [8.16](#b-01496) on the scalar bilinears, and the translation component $P_1$. Two features carry the content. The obstruction with three legs has a component outside the image of $Q$ on cubic functionals, and the quadratic counterterm of Chapter 4 matches it exactly, which is the Wess–Zumino condition of this sector; and because $(Q^{GF})^2\neq0$ in Feynman gauge (Proposition [3.5](#b-00397)), $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ also enters cycles as a composite line from $A|_V$ to $c$, which adds to $D_1$ a multiple of the classical transformation that the two-point equations leave free and the arity-two equation along $(\Delta,P_b)$ fixes when the one-loop quantisation and the local representatives exist through arity two (Theorem [9.31](#b-01869)).

The unit is $\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$, and every coefficient below is an element of $\mathbb Q+\mathbb Q\log\tfrac32$ times it. The obstruction and the finite counterterm are written with their factor $\hbar$: a one-loop quantisation is a finite counterterm $\hbar F_1$ with $s(\hbar F_1)=\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}$, $s=d_{CE}+Q+\{I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)},-\}$ (Theorem [8.8](#b-01457)), and both sides are multiples of the unit. For a cochain $f$, $f^{(0)}$ is its arity-zero part and $f^{(1)}(x)$ its arity-one part evaluated on $x\in\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$, as in Definition [8.16](#b-01496). An identity between functionals in a sector, a prescribed list of legs, is the identity between their parts with these legs; for a quadratic functional $X$ the part of $\{I,X\}$ with three legs is the bracket with the cubic part of $I$ in [(1.3)](#b-00159). Every functional containing $\lambda$ or $\lambda^*$ is also given in the two-component form of Definition [8.1](#b-01405) (Remarks [9.13](#b-01747) and [9.27](#b-01846)); Weinberg's form follows from ${\not d}=\gamma_W^\mu\partial_\mu$ on the Dirac column (Proposition [8.2](#b-01418)).
9.1 The cubic sector of the one-loop obstruction

With the finite counterterm of Theorem [4.32](#b-00868) the obstruction vanishes in the sector $(c,A|_V)$ (Theorem [4.30](#b-00858)). The sectors with three legs of Remark [4.34](#b-00876) come next: this section fixes a basis, computes the obstruction class of graphs by class of graphs, and solves the equation for the cubic finite counterterm.
Definition 9.1 (Bases of the three-leg functionals).

With $(-,-)$ the pairing of $\mathfrak g$ tensored with the metric, $d^*d$ and $dd^*$ acting on the one-form $A|_V$, and $d^*d$ acting on each scalar $\iota_wA$, $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, the functionals of degree $1$ are
with the pairings of the terms $(dc,A^*)$ and $\tfrac12(\lambda,{\not d}\lambda)$ of the action in $G_4$ and $G_5$, and the functionals of degree $0$ are

together with $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_V,\lambda]))$ and $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\lambda]))$, whose sum is twice the cubic term $\tfrac12\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,({\not d}_A-{\not d})\lambda)$ of $I$. In $H_2$ the one-form $d(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ and the one-form $[A|_V,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}]$ are paired with the metrics of $V$ and of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$.
Lemma 9.2 (Leg sets and colour).

A local functional of degree $1$ with three legs and Weyl weight at most $4$, invariant under translations, $\mathrm{Spin}(4,\mathbb C)\times\mathrm{Spin}(6,\mathbb C)$ and the adjoint action of $\mathfrak g$, has one of the leg sets
(c,A|_V,A|_V),\qquad(c,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}),\qquad(c,\lambda,\lambda),\qquad(c,c,A^*|_V),
and its colour factor is a multiple of $(X_0,[X_1,X_2])$, $X_j$ the $\mathfrak g$-factor of leg $j$. Every one-loop colour factor of these sectors reduces to it through
\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y\mathrm{ad}_Z)=\tfrac12\,\frac{\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{(X,Y)}\,(X,[Y,Z]) .
Proof.

The functional degrees are $+1$ for $c$, $0$ for $A$ and $\lambda$, $-1$ for $A^*$ and $\lambda^*$, $-2$ for $c^*$, and the Weyl weights are $0,1,\tfrac32,3,\tfrac52,4$ (Definition [6.1](#b-01067)). Degree $1$ with three legs means
n_c-n_{A^*}-n_{\lambda^*}-2n_{c^*}=1,\qquad n_c+n_A+n_\lambda+n_{A^*}+n_{\lambda^*}+n_{c^*}=3,

solved by one $c$ with two legs among $A$, $\lambda$, and by two $c$ with one $A^*$ or one $\lambda^*$. A single spinor leg ($cA\lambda$, $cc\lambda^*$) is odd under $-1\in\mathrm{Spin}(4,\mathbb C)$, and a single vector of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ ($cA|_VA|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $ccA^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$) admits no $\mathrm{Spin}(6,\mathbb C)$-invariant pairing. The remaining leg sets have the weights $2,2,3,3$. A tree contraction of vertices of $I$ gives $([X_0,X_1],X_2)$. A one-loop colour factor is a trace of products of $\mathrm{ad}$'s; the invariance of $(-,-)$ gives $\mathrm{ad}_X^{T}=-\mathrm{ad}_X$, hence $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y\mathrm{ad}_Z)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Z\mathrm{ad}_Y)=\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_{[Y,Z]})$, which is the stated identity; a bubble with a quartic vertex gives $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_{X_i}\mathrm{ad}_{[X_j,X_k]})$. ∎
Proposition 9.3 (Basis of the sectors).

Write $f=([X_0,X_1],X_2)$, $p_j$ for the momentum of leg $j$ (leg $0$ is the first $c$), $a_j\in V$, $w_j\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, $b\in V$ and $\lambda_j\in\Sigma$ for the fibre elements, and take plane-wave values as in Definition [1.13](#b-00162).
• (ii) $(c,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ has dimension $1$, with $G_3=f\,(w_1,w_2)(|p_2|^2-|p_1|^2)$.

• (iii) $(c,\lambda,\lambda)$ is spanned by $G_5=-if\,(\lambda_1,\rho(p_0)\lambda_2)$ and the parity-odd structure $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,\lambda],{\not d}\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)\lambda)$, of value $if\,(\lambda_1,\rho(p_2-p_1)\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)\lambda_2)$, $v_1,\dots,v_4$ an oriented orthonormal basis of $V$ (Proposition [1.2](#b-00068)).
• (iv) $(c,c,A^*|_V)$ has dimension $1$, with $G_4=-if\,(p_2,b)$.
• (v) The functionals $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,A|_V],A|_V)$ and $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}],A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ of weight $2$ vanish, and weight $3$ carries no invariant.
The parity-odd structure has coefficient $0$ in every functional built from $S$, $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$, $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$, $K_\varepsilon$ and $K_0$.
Proof.

Relabelling two identical legs leaves a functional unchanged: for two legs $A$ its value is symmetric under their exchange, for two odd legs antisymmetric, since $r_ir_j=-r_jr_i$. The colour factor $f$ is antisymmetric under $1\leftrightarrow2$ and under $0\leftrightarrow1$, so the kinematic factor is antisymmetric under $(p_1,a_1)\leftrightarrow(p_2,a_2)$ for $(c,A,A)$ and symmetric for $(c,\lambda,\lambda)$ and $(c,c,A^*|_V)$. In $(c,A|_V,A|_V)$ at weight $4$ it is bilinear in $a_1,a_2$ and quadratic in $p_1,p_2$; the antisymmetric parity-even combinations are $(a_1,a_2)(|p_1|^2-|p_2|^2)$ and $(a_1,p_1)(a_2,p_1)-(a_1,p_2)(a_2,p_2)$, on which $(G_1,G_2)$ has the invertible matrix $\begin{pmatrix}-1&1\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, from $d^*d\mapsto|p|^2-p\,(p,-)$ and $dd^*\mapsto p\,(p,-)$ on the second $A|_V$; the parity-odd $(a_1\wedge a_2\wedge p_1\wedge p_2,\,v_1\wedge v_2\wedge v_3\wedge v_4)$ is symmetric. In $(c,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$, $\mathrm{Spin}(6,\mathbb C)$ admits $(w_1,w_2)$ alone. In $(c,\lambda,\lambda)$ the invariant bilinears of two elements of $\Sigma$ and one vector $q\in V$ are $(\lambda_1,\rho(q)\lambda_2)$, symmetric in $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$, and $(\lambda_1,\rho(q)\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)\lambda_2)$, antisymmetric (Proposition [1.2](#b-00068)); the symmetric combinations are $q=p_1+p_2=-p_0$ in the first and $q=p_2-p_1$ in the second. In $(c,c,A^*|_V)$ the symmetric combination is $(b,p_0+p_1)=-(b,p_2)$. At weight $2$ the factor $(a_1,a_2)$, resp. $(w_1,w_2)$, is symmetric, and at weight $3$ the leg sets admit no invariant (Lemma [4.19](#b-00726)). Let an element of $\mathrm{Spin}(10,\mathbb C)$ lift the product of the reflections in one direction of $V$ and one direction of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$. It preserves the action, $Q$, $Q^{GF}$ and $H$, hence every kernel and counterterm, fixes $G_5$ and maps $\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)$ to $-\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)$, since $v_1$ anticommutes with $v_2,v_3,v_4$ and the direction of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ commutes with all four; so the parity-odd coefficient vanishes. ∎
Proposition 9.4 (The maps $Q$ and $\{I,-\}$).

• (i) $QH_1=-2G_1$, $QH_2=-G_3$, $QH_3=-\tfrac12G_1-G_4$, $QH_4=-\tfrac12G_3$, $QH_5=G_5$, $QH_6=2G_4$, $Q\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_V,\lambda]))=-2G_5$ and $Q\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\lambda]))=0$. The cubic part of $I$ is $-\tfrac14H_1-\tfrac12H_2+\tfrac12\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A,\lambda]))+H_3+H_4+H_5+\tfrac12H_6$, and its image under $Q$ vanishes.

• (ii) $H_1,\dots,H_6$, $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_V,\lambda]))$ and $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\lambda]))$ span the parity-even invariant local functionals of degree $0$, Weyl weight $4$ and three legs. On their span $Q$ has rank $4$ and image $\mathrm{span}\{G_1,G_3,G_4,G_5\}$, and its kernel is spanned by
H_1-4H_3-2H_6,\qquad H_2-2H_4,\qquad \int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_V,\lambda]))+2H_5,\qquad \int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\lambda])).

Every invariant local functional of degree $-1$ with three legs has Weyl weight at least $6$, so these four functionals represent four independent classes of the cohomology of $Q$ on local functionals of weight $4$.
• (iii) In the sectors with three legs, with $H=d^*d+dd^*$ the componentwise Laplacian of Proposition [3.5](#b-00397) (the functionals $H_j$ carry an index),
Proof.

(i) $Q$ acts by $F(e+rQe)=F(e)+r\,(QF)(e)$ with $r$ odd [C07, §6.2], that is by the substitutions $A|_V\mapsto A|_V-r\,dc$, $A^*\mapsto A^*-\tfrac r2d^*dA$, $c^*\mapsto c^*+r\,d^*(A^*|_V)$, $\lambda^*\mapsto\lambda^*+r\,{\not d}\lambda$ (Proposition [1.11](#b-00135)), with $r$ moved to the left. For $H_1$ the cubic term gives $-2r[A|_V\wedge dc]$, and with $d[A,c]=[dA,c]-[A\wedge dc]$ and $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(dA,[dA,c])=0$,
QH_1=-2\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(dA|_V,[A|_V\wedge dc])=2\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([A|_V,c],d^*dA|_V)=-2G_1 .

For $H_3$ the substitution in $A|_V$ gives $-\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([dc,c],A^*|_V)=-G_4$, since $[dc,c]=[c,dc]$ for the odd $c$, and the substitution in $A^*|_V$ gives $\tfrac12\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([A|_V,c],d^*dA|_V)=-\tfrac12G_1$; $H_4$ receives the second step alone, $H_5$ gives $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,\lambda],{\not d}\lambda)$, and $H_6$ gives $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(d[c,c],A^*)=2G_4$. For the Yukawa-type functionals, $Q$ hits the $A|_V$ slot alone, and with the symmetry of $(\lambda_1,\rho(v)[Y,\lambda_2])$ in $\lambda_1,\lambda_2$,
Q\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([A|_V,\lambda]))=\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,\rho([dc,\lambda]))=-2\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,\lambda],{\not d}\lambda)=-2G_5 .

The cubic part of $I$ follows from $(dA,[A\wedge A])=(dA|_V,[A|_V\wedge A|_V])+2(dA|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},[A|_V,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}])$, and its image is $(\tfrac12G_1+\tfrac12G_3)-G_5+(-\tfrac12G_1-G_4)-\tfrac12G_3+G_5+G_4=0$, the cubic part of the classical master equation (Proposition [1.14](#b-00173)).

(ii) Degree $0$, three legs and weight $4$ leave $(A,A,A)$ with one derivative, and $(A,\lambda,\lambda)$, $(c,A,A^*)$, $(c,\lambda,\lambda^*)$, $(c,c,c^*)$ without derivatives. For $(A|_V)^3$ the parity-even invariant is $H_1$, and the parity-odd one is the cubic part of the total derivative $(F_A\wedge F_A)$; for $A|_V(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})^2$ the invariants agree up to integration by parts with $H_2$; three vectors of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ admit no invariant. For $(A,\lambda,\lambda)$ the kinematic factor is symmetric in the two $\lambda$ legs, as in Proposition [9.3](#b-01659): with $a\in V$ this leaves $(\lambda_1,\rho(a)\lambda_2)$, and with $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, which commutes with $v_1v_2v_3v_4$, it leaves $(\lambda_1,\rho(w)\lambda_2)$ and the parity-odd $(\lambda_1,\rho(w)\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)\lambda_2)$. The remaining leg sets give $H_3$, $H_4$, $H_5$ with a parity-odd partner $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,\lambda],\rho(v_1v_2v_3v_4)\lambda^*)$, and $H_6$. The rank and the kernel follow from (i). Degree $-1$ with three legs requires an antifield; a single spinor leg or a single vector index of $V$ or of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$ admits no invariant, and $\lambda^*\otimes\lambda$, $\lambda^*\otimes\lambda^*$ contain no invariant vector or scalar, so the invariant leg sets of degree $-1$ have weight at least $6$, the lowest being $(A^*,\lambda,\lambda)$ and $(A^*|_V,A^*|_V,c)$; the image under $Q$ of the functionals of degree $-1$, weight $4$ and three legs is therefore zero, and the four kernel elements represent independent classes.

(iii) In the cubic part of $I$ the antifields enter linearly, with $\partial_{A^*}=-[A,c]$, $\partial_{\lambda^*}=[c,\lambda]$, $\partial_{c^*}=\tfrac12[c,c]$ (left derivatives; the first sign from moving $A^*$ across $[A,c]$). By Definition [1.6](#b-00095), for $X$ a functional of $A$ alone $\{I,X\}=-\frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0}X(A+t[A,c])$ with the odd factor to the left, and for $X$ a functional of $\lambda$ alone $\{I,X\}$ is the derivative of $X$ along $\lambda\mapsto[c,\lambda]$. Integration by parts gives the first three brackets, $\{I,\int(A,A)\}=-2\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([A,c],A)=0$ and $\{I,\int(A,HA)\}=-2\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([A,c],HA)=2(G_1+G_2+G_3)$; for $\lambda$, $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,\lambda],{\not d}\lambda)-\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,{\not d}[c,\lambda])=2G_5$. For $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(dc,A^*)$ the bracket consists of the parts of $Q$ applied to the cubic part of $I$ coming from the substitutions in $A|_V$ and in $c^*$: $(\tfrac12G_1+\tfrac12G_3-G_5-G_4)+G_4$. ∎
Corollary 9.5 (Completions).
In the sectors with three legs, $Q$ of the second entry plus the bracket of $I$ with the first entry vanishes for each of the pairs

the quadratic and cubic parts of $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(F_{A|_V},F_{A|_V})$, $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(d_{A|_V}A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},d_{A|_V}A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$, $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\lambda,{\not d}_A\lambda)$ and of the antifield part $\int\mathrm{dvol}\big((d_Ac,A^*)+([c,\lambda],\lambda^*)+\tfrac12([c,c],c^*)\big)$ of $S$. In the third pair $\int(\lambda,\rho([A,\lambda]))$ may be replaced by $-2H_5$; the two choices differ by the $Q$-closed $\int(\lambda,\rho([A,\lambda]))+2H_5$.
Proof.

By Proposition [9.4](#b-01669): $-2G_1+2G_1=0$, $-2G_3+2G_3=0$, $-2G_5+2G_5=0$ and $(-\tfrac12G_1-G_4)-\tfrac12G_3+G_5+G_4+\tfrac12G_1+\tfrac12G_3-G_5=0$. The functionals are the stated parts by $F_{A|_V}=dA|_V+\tfrac12[A|_V\wedge A|_V]$, $d_{A|_V}A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}=d(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})+[A|_V,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}]$, ${\not d}_A\lambda={\not d}\lambda+\rho([A,\lambda])$ and $d_Ac=dc+[A,c]$. ∎
Lemma 9.6 (The sector $(c,c,A|_V)$).
On the sector $(c,c,A|_V)$ of degree $2$, $QG_1=QG_3=QG_4=QG_5=0$,
QG_2=\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,dc],dd^*A|_V)+\int\mathrm{dvol}\,([c,A|_V],dd^*dc)\neq0,\qquad \Big\{I,\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(d^*dc,d^*A|_V)\Big\}=QG_2 .
Proof.

$[c,dc]=\tfrac12d[c,c]$ and $d^*d^*=0$ give $QG_1=0$ and $QG_4=0$; $Q$ hits no slot of $G_3$ and $G_5$; in $G_2$ the substitution $A|_V\mapsto A|_V-r\,dc$ hits both $A|_V$. The plane-wave value of $QG_2$ is $-if\,r_0r_1\big(|p_0|^2(p_0,b)+|p_1|^2(p_1,b)+|p_2|^2(p_2,b)\big)$, nonzero. For the bracket, $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(d^*dc,d^*A|_V)=Q\big(-\tfrac12\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(d^*A|_V,d^*A|_V)\big)$, and by the Jacobi identity and Proposition [9.4](#b-01669) (i), $\{I,QF\}=-Q\{I,F\}$ in the sector, so the bracket is $-Q\big(-\tfrac12\cdot2G_2\big)=QG_2$. ∎
Proposition 9.7 (Graph classes).

By Proposition [4.26](#b-00828) and [(4.8)](#b-00839), the part with three legs of the order-$\hbar$ term of $Q\,W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon])$ is the sum of the following classes of graphs, the special edge carrying $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ between a field and its antifield ($A|_V$–$A^*|_V$, $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$–$A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$–$\lambda^*$, $c$–$c^*$) and the other edges $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$:
• (i) cycle graphs: the special edge on the cycle of a triangle of three cubic vertices or of a bubble of one quartic and one cubic vertex;
• (ii) bridge graphs: the special edge joins a cubic vertex with two external legs to a one-loop two-point subgraph;
• (iii) the counterterm vertex $-Q\,I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$;

• (iv) the counterterm bracket $-\{I,I^{CT}[\varepsilon]\}_\varepsilon$, with the cubic part of $I$ and the quadratic part of $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$, split into its part with $K_0$ and its part with $K_\varepsilon-K_0$;

• (v) reducible graphs: a defect subgraph with two legs, one of the bubbles (a)–(e) of Theorem [4.30](#b-00858) or the vertex $-Q\,I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ with two legs, joined by an edge $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ to a cubic vertex with two external legs.
Proof.

The vertex $\tfrac12(\{I,I\}_\varepsilon-\{I,I\})$ has order $\hbar^0$, so its graphs have one cycle; the other terms of [(4.8)](#b-00839) have order $\hbar$, so their graphs are trees, and $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon I=0$ (proof of Theorem [4.30](#b-00858)). If the special edge lies on the cycle, a cycle of $n$ vertices of valence at least three carries at least $n$ further half-edges; with three legs, and every tree hanging off the cycle carrying at least two legs, the cycle is a triangle of cubic vertices, a quartic-cubic bubble, or a cubic-cubic bubble with one half-edge joined to a cubic vertex with two legs, which is class (v). If the special edge is a bridge, its tree side has at least two legs: two legs at one cubic vertex and a two-point one-loop side, class (ii), or three legs and a one-point side, which vanishes by Lemma [4.7](#b-00615). The trees are $-Q\,I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ with three legs, $-Q\,I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ with two legs joined to a cubic vertex, and $-\{I,I^{CT}[\varepsilon]\}_\varepsilon$; the brackets of the quartic part of $I$ with the quadratic counterterm and of the cubic part of $I$ with the cubic counterterm have four legs. ∎

Proposition 9.8 (Limits of the bridge and reducible graphs).

• (i) The sum of the bridge graphs and of the counterterm bracket with $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ tends to $0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. Separately, the counterterm bracket with $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ tends to $\tfrac94\{I,\int(A,HA)\}=\tfrac92(G_1+G_2+G_3)$ units and the bridge graphs tend to the opposite.

• (ii) The reducible graphs tend to the tree with one vertex given by the quadratic part of $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}$, one cubic vertex of $I$ and one edge $P(0,\infty)$, which is the local functional
\Big(\tfrac{27}8G_1-\tfrac{27}8G_2+\tfrac{27}8G_3-\tfrac{27}4G_4-\tfrac{27}4G_5\Big)\ \text{units}.
Proof.

(i) Removing the bridge separates a bridge graph into the cubic vertex and a connected one-loop two-point graph of $W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),I)$; summed with their weights, the bridge graphs are the cross terms of $\tfrac12\{W,W\}$ built with $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ between the cubic part of $I$ and the one-loop two-point part of $W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),I)$. In momentum space $K_\varepsilon-K_0=(e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1)K_0$, $p$ the momentum through the bridge, so the bridge graphs and the counterterm bracket with $K_\varepsilon-K_0$ add up to $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$ times the bracket of the cubic part of $I$ with the renormalised two-point function at $p$. The latter has a limit at $p\neq0$ (Theorem [4.16](#b-00707), Proposition [4.8](#b-00628)), which gives the first statement. In the counterterm bracket alone, the $\log\varepsilon$ terms of $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ give $(e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1)\log\varepsilon\to0$, and the mass term gives, with $\varepsilon^{-1}(e^{-\varepsilon H}-1)\to-H$ and Proposition [9.4](#b-01669) (iii),
-\tfrac94\varepsilon^{-1}\Big\{I,\int\mathrm{dvol}\,\big(A,(e^{-\varepsilon H}-1)A\big)\Big\}\longrightarrow\tfrac94\Big\{I,\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(A,HA)\Big\}=\tfrac92(G_1+G_2+G_3).

(ii) The reducible graphs form the tree with one vertex given by the defect graphs with two legs and one cubic vertex of $I$, joined by $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$. By Lemma [4.29](#b-00852) and Theorem [4.30](#b-00858), at fixed $p\neq0$ the defect graphs with two legs equal the quadratic part of $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}$ at $p$ plus $O(\varepsilon)$, their coefficients of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ cancelling, and the edge carries $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}$ times $P(0,\infty)$ at $p$; both factors converge. The quadratic part of $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}$ is $-\tfrac{27}8\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(c,d^*dd^*A|_V)$ units: through the $A|_V$ line the factor $|p|^2$ of $d^*d$ on $c$, and through the $c$–$A^*$ line the factor $|p|^2$ of $d^*d$ on $A|_V$, cancels the factor $|p|^{-2}$ of $P(0,\infty)$, so the tree is local, and its evaluation with the components of Proposition [3.11](#b-00430) gives the stated functional. ∎
Theorem 9.9 (Singular parts).

• (i) Each cycle graph has the value $\varepsilon^{-\omega/2}$ times a first coefficient plus a second coefficient plus $O(\varepsilon\log\varepsilon)$, where, in the scaled Schwinger times $\tau_1\in[0,1]$ of the special edge and $\tau_2,\tau_3\in[1,\infty)$, the two coefficients are the integrals of the Taylor coefficients of order $0$ and of order $\omega$ in the external momenta of the Gaussian-integrated integrand, $\omega=2$ for $(c,A,A)$ and $\omega=1$ for $(c,\lambda,\lambda)$ and $(c,c,A^*|_V)$. These integrals converge, the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ vanishes, and the coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ vanishes after the sum over the graphs of a row.

• (ii) The counterterm vertex and the counterterm bracket with $K_0$ are multiples of $\log\varepsilon$, with the coefficients of the second table below, and their sum vanishes in every sector: with the unit times the field-counting functional $2\int(A,A^*)-4\int(\lambda^*,\lambda)-\int(c^*,c)$ of Chapter 6, the sum is minus $Q$ of the bracket of $I$ with this functional minus the bracket of $I$ with its image under $Q$, which is zero.
• (iii) In every sector with three legs the coefficients of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ and of $\log\varepsilon$ of the order-$\hbar$ term of $Q\,W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon])$ vanish.
Proof.

(i) The special edge carries $-\int_0^\varepsilon|q|^2e^{-t|q|^2}dt$ times the components of $K_0$ (Proposition [4.27](#b-00837)). The superficial degree $\omega$ is the total momentum degree of the vertex functions and of the numerators of the edges $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ for triangles, and that degree plus $2$ for bubbles, and after the substitution $t_e=\varepsilon\tau_e$ the Taylor coefficient of order $j$ in the external momenta carries $\varepsilon^{(j-\omega)/2}$. For odd $j<\omega$ it is Lorentz-odd and vanishes; for $j=0$ it is $\varepsilon^{-\omega/2}$ times a functional of weight $4-\omega$: for $\omega=2$ it vanishes after the symmetrisation over the identical legs, and for $\omega=1$ the leg sets carry no invariant of weight $3$ (Proposition [9.3](#b-01659) (v)). For a triangle, on $\tau_2,\tau_3\ge R$ the Gaussian integral over the loop momentum gives $(\tau_1+\tau_2+\tau_3)^{-2}$ times monomials of total degree $\omega+2$ in the loop momentum and the external momenta, so the coefficient of order $j$ is bounded by a multiple of $R^{-2-(\omega+2-j)/2}$, and the shell $R\le\tau_2+\tau_3\le2R$ contributes at most a multiple of $R^{-(\omega+2-j)/2}$, summable over dyadic $R$ for $j<\omega+2$; for bubbles the exponent $\tau_1\tau_2|p|^2/(\tau_1+\tau_2)$ is at most $|p|^2$, uniformly in $\tau_2$ (Lemma [4.29](#b-00852)). The order $\omega+1$ is Lorentz-odd, and the orders $\omega+2$ and beyond contribute $O(\varepsilon\log\varepsilon)$. (ii) By Theorem [4.22](#b-00805), the cubic part of $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is $\log\varepsilon$ times the bracket of $I$ with the unit times the field-counting functional (the multiples $6,6,10,10,1,1,1,1$ of the cubic vertices), with coefficient $0$ of $\varepsilon^{-1}$, and the quadratic $\log\varepsilon$ part is $\log\varepsilon$ times the image under $Q$ of the same functional. With Proposition [9.4](#b-01669) the counterterm vertex gives, vertex by vertex, $-3G_1$ from $(A|_V)^3$ and $+\tfrac12G_1$ from $A|_VcA^*|_V$; $-3G_3$ and $+\tfrac12G_3$ from $A|_V(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})^2$ and $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}cA^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$; $+10G_5$ and $-G_5$ from $\lambda\lambda A|_V$ and $c\lambda\lambda^*$; $+G_4$ and $-G_4$ from $A|_VcA^*|_V$ and $ccc^*$; and the counterterm bracket with $K_0$ gives $+\tfrac12G_1+2G_1$, $+\tfrac12G_3+2G_3$, $-G_5-8G_5$ and $-G_4+G_4$. Their sum is minus $Q$ of the bracket of $I$ with that functional minus the bracket of $I$ with its image under $Q$, which vanishes by the Jacobi identity and the vanishing image under $Q$ of the cubic part of $I$. The mass term contributes $\{I,\int(A,A)\}=0$. (iii) follows from (i), (ii) and Proposition [9.8](#b-01707). ∎

Theorem 9.10 (The cubic part of the obstruction).
In the sectors with three legs,

\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}=\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}\Big[\big(\tfrac{11}4+\tfrac{19}4\log\tfrac32\big)(G_1+G_3)+\tfrac{27}8G_2-9\log\tfrac32\,G_5\Big], \tag{9.1}
the sum of the totals of the table of cycle graphs. The coefficient of $G_4$ and that of the parity-odd structure of $(c,\lambda,\lambda)$ vanish.
Proof.

By Definition [8.7](#b-01453) with the finite counterterm set to zero, the part with three legs of the order-$\hbar$ term of $\lim_{\varepsilon\to0}Q\,W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon])$ is the part with three legs of the tree-level flow of $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}$: the cubic part of $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}$ plus the tree of Proposition [9.8](#b-01707) (ii). By Proposition [9.7](#b-01695) the limit is the sum of the five classes. By Proposition [9.8](#b-01707) the bridge graphs cancel against the counterterm bracket with $K_\varepsilon-K_0$, and the reducible graphs give the tree; by Theorem [9.9](#b-01715) the counterterm vertex and the counterterm bracket with $K_0$ are multiples of $\log\varepsilon$ that cancel. The cubic part of $\hbar\,\mathrm{Ob}^{(0)}$ is therefore the limit of the cycle graphs, the totals of the table. The parity-odd coefficient vanishes by Proposition [9.3](#b-01659). ∎

The part with three legs of $s\,\mathrm{Ob}=0$ (Theorem [8.8](#b-01457) (i)) at arity zero is

with the coefficient $-\tfrac{27}8$ of the quadratic part (Theorem [4.30](#b-00858)). The coefficients $\alpha_1,\alpha_3,\alpha_4,\alpha_5$ enter it with coefficient $0$, and the computed value $\alpha_2=\tfrac{27}8$ satisfies it. Remark 9.14 (Method of computation).

The value of each cycle graph is an exact element of $\mathbb Q+\mathbb Q\log\tfrac32$: the coefficient of $\varepsilon^0$ of Theorem [9.9](#b-01715) reduces to master integrals over the scaled Schwinger region, evaluated in closed form, and each multilinear form is decomposed on the basis of Proposition [9.3](#b-01659) by exact evaluation on integer plane waves in explicit realisations of $V_{10}$, $\Sigma$ over $\mathbb Q(i)$ and $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(2)$, as in Remark [4.36](#b-00889); the colour reduction of Lemma [9.2](#b-01650) makes the result valid for every simple $\mathfrak g$. The rows are organised by the census of Proposition [9.7](#b-01695); the complete order-$\hbar$ sums at finite $\varepsilon$ in the sectors $(c,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ and $(c,c,A^*|_V)$ have the limits $\alpha_3$, $\alpha_4$ and the reducible tree.
9.2 Closed forms along the dilatation

Along $\Delta$ the generator $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ is quadratic (Example [2.13](#b-00317)), and the regulator moves under it through its two endpoints (Proposition [7.10](#b-01286) at $T=\infty$, Proposition [9.21](#b-01800) at finite $T$). The graphs with one vertex $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ therefore have closed forms at finite $\varepsilon$ and $T$. In this section and the next two, $v=2E$, so that $v.$ is the operator of Lemma [7.5](#b-01234) on all slots, and $P(\varepsilon,T)\star=\int_\varepsilon^TQ^{GF}e^{-tH}dt$ is the operator represented by $P(\varepsilon,T)$ (Definition [8.3](#b-01429)). For an operator $X$ on $\mathscr E$ the kernel $(X\otimes1)K_0$ represents $X$, so $P(\varepsilon,T)=(P(\varepsilon,T)\star\otimes1)K_0$. The operator $\partial_\phi$ is read as in Definition [3.10](#b-00427): on the product of a coordinate functional of the first factor and one of the second, in this order, it is the corresponding component of $\phi$. A linear operator $X$ on $\mathscr E$ acts on functionals as the derivation induced by $\ell\mapsto\ell\circ X$ on linear functionals $\ell$ [C07, §6.2], as $Q$ does, and $XF$ denotes this derivation applied to $F$. For a functional $F$ and an even $J$, the linearised flow of $F$ at $J$ is $e^{-W(P(\varepsilon,T),J)/\hbar}e^{\hbar\partial_{P(\varepsilon,T)}}\big(F\,e^{J/\hbar}\big)$; for even $F$ it is $\partial_\delta W(P(\varepsilon,T),J+\delta F)$ with $\delta$ a square-zero parameter of degree $0$, as in [(7.1)](#b-01251).
Lemma 9.15 (Operators and kernels).
For a kernel $\phi\in\mathscr E\otimes\mathscr E$ and a linear operator $X$ on $\mathscr E$, of either parity,
[\partial_\phi,X]=\partial_{(X\otimes1+1\otimes X)\phi} \tag{9.3}

as a graded commutator of operators on functionals; for $X=Q$ this is [C07, §6.4]. If $X$ is even and preserves $\langle\,,\rangle$, then $(1\otimes X)K_0=-(X\otimes1)K_0$, and $(1\otimes Q^{GF})K_0=(Q^{GF}\otimes1)K_0$; the same holds with any function of $H$ in place of $Q^{GF}$.
Proof.

Both sides of [(9.3)](#b-01757) are second-order operators with constant coefficients, determined by their values on products $\ell_1\ell_2$ of linear functionals. On such a product $\partial_\phi$ gives the constant $(\ell_1\otimes\ell_2)(\phi)$, on which $X$ vanishes, and $X(\ell_1\ell_2)=(\ell_1\circ X)\ell_2+(-1)^{|X||\ell_1|}\ell_1(\ell_2\circ X)$, so the left side gives $(\ell_1\otimes\ell_2)\big((X\otimes1+1\otimes X)\phi\big)$, the sign being the Koszul sign of $X$ passing $\ell_1$. Preservation of the pairing by an even $X$ is $(X\otimes1+1\otimes X)K_0=0$, as in Proposition [7.6](#b-01244); for $Q^{GF}$ the identity is Proposition [3.3](#b-00383), and $H$ is symmetric for the pairing. ∎
Lemma 9.16 (Brackets with $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$).

• (i) For every functional $F$, $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),F\}=v.F$: the sign of Definition [7.4](#b-01226) is $+1$. For a local functional $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\text{density})$ of Weyl weight $k$ (fields plus derivatives) $v.$ multiplies it by $2(k-4)$, and for a local operator $O$ of Weyl weight $w_O$, $v.O=2(E+w_O)O$ (Proposition [6.18](#b-01202)).
• (iii) $Q\,S^{(1)}(\Delta)=0$, $\{I,S^{(1)}(\Delta)\}=0$ and $\partial_{P(\varepsilon,T)}S^{(1)}(\Delta)=0$.
• (iv) For every functional $F$, $\partial_{P(\varepsilon,T)}\big(S^{(1)}(\Delta)F\big)-S^{(1)}(\Delta)\,\partial_{P(\varepsilon,T)}F=\big(P(\varepsilon,T)\star\,v.\big)F$.
Proof.

(i) By Definition [1.6](#b-00095) and the proof of Lemma [4.21](#b-00796), the bracket is at each position that of [C07, §10.1] for a point, with $\Delta_0=\sum\partial_{x_i}\partial_{\xi_i}$ over the even members $x_i$ and their odd partners $\xi_i$. For a number $a$,
\{a\,x_i\xi_i,x_i\}=\Delta_0(a\,x_i^2\xi_i)-\Delta_0(a\,x_i\xi_i)\,x_i=a\,x_i,\qquad \{a\,x_i\xi_i,\xi_i\}=-a\,\xi_i .

The terms of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ (Example [2.13](#b-00317)) are of this form: $(v.A,A^*)$ with the even member first, and $-(v.\lambda,\lambda^*)$, $-(v.c,c^*)$ with the even members $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ paired against the image of the partner. With the action of $v.$ on the antifields of Definition [7.4](#b-01226), the bracket sends every coordinate functional $\ell$ to $\ell\circ v.$, and it is a derivation [C07, Lemma 4.3.2]. Since $[E,\partial_m]=-\partial_m$, $v.$ multiplies a monomial of Weyl weight $k$ by $2E+2k$, and $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,E(\cdot)=-4\int\mathrm{dvol}\,(\cdot)$. (ii) $\{-,-\}_t$ is built from $K_t=(e^{-tH}\otimes1)K_0$ (Definition [3.15](#b-00457)), which replaces the contracted leg of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ by its image under $e^{-tH}$. (iii) $Q\,S^{(1)}(\Delta)=\{\tfrac12\langle e,Qe\rangle,S^{(1)}(\Delta)\}$ (Proposition [1.11](#b-00135)) is, up to sign, $v.$ of $\tfrac12\langle e,Qe\rangle$, which vanishes by $[v.,Q]=0$ and the preservation of the pairing (Proposition [7.10](#b-01286)); $\{I,S^{(1)}(\Delta)\}$ is, up to sign, $v.I=0$, every density of $I$ having Weyl weight $4$; and $P(\varepsilon,T)$ has no component in the slot pairs $A\otimes A^*$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda^*$, $c\otimes c^*$ of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ (Proposition [3.11](#b-00430)). (iv) The left side contracts one leg of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ with one leg of $F$ through $P(\varepsilon,T)$; it is a derivation of $F$, and on a linear functional $\ell$ it gives $\ell\circ(P(\varepsilon,T)\star v.)$, the antifield leg of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ being contracted and its field leg carrying $v.$. ∎
Definition 9.17 (The composite kernel).

For $0<\varepsilon<T\le\infty$ the composite kernel is $\big(P(\varepsilon,T)\star\,v.\otimes1+1\otimes P(\varepsilon,T)\star\,v.\big)P(\varepsilon,T)$: the two legs of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ joined, in both orders, to two edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$.
Proposition 9.18 (The composite kernel).
Write $P=P(\varepsilon,T)$.

• (i) The composite kernel equals $2\big(P\star\,v.\,P\star\otimes1\big)K_0$, the kernel of the even operator $2P\star\,v.\,P\star=v.\,(P\star)^2+(P\star)^2\,v.$, with $(P\star)^2=(Q^{GF})^2\big(\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt\big)^2$; it has degree $-1$.

• (ii) Its components lie in $c\otimes A|_V$ and $A|_V\otimes c$: in a graph it joins a leg $c$ to a leg $A|_V$. It is nonzero because $(Q^{GF})^2A^*=2\,d^*(A^*|_V)$ and $(Q^{GF})^2c^*=-2\,dc^*$ (Proposition [3.5](#b-00397)).

• (iii) $Q\,P\star+P\star\,Q=e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH}$ and $Q\,(P\star\,v.\,P\star)=(P\star\,v.\,P\star)\,Q$. Hence $(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)$ annihilates the composite kernel, and $\partial$ of the composite kernel anticommutes with $Q$.

• (iv) At $T=\infty$, in momentum space, $(P\star)^2=(Q^{GF})^2e^{-2\varepsilon|p|^2}|p|^{-4}$; on the slot of $A^*|_V$ it is of order $|p|^{-3}$ as $p\to0$, and so is the composite kernel, $v.$ acting as an Euler operator plus constants. At finite $T$, $(P\star)^2$ is bounded by a multiple of $T^2|p|$.
Proof.
(i) $(P\star v.\otimes1)P=(P\star v.P\star\otimes1)K_0$. For the second term, the Koszul sign of two odd operators on different factors and Lemma [9.15](#b-01755) give

(1\otimes P\star v.)(P\star\otimes1)K_0=-(P\star\otimes1)(1\otimes Q^{GF})\Big(1\otimes\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt\Big)(1\otimes v.)K_0=(P\star\otimes1)(v.\,P\star\otimes1)K_0=(P\star v.P\star\otimes1)K_0 .

By Proposition [7.10](#b-01286), $[v.,Q^{GF}]=-4Q^{GF}$ and $[v.,H]=-4H$, so for a function of $H$ the commutator with $v.$ is $-4H$ times its derivative in $H$, and $[v.,P\star]$ is $Q^{GF}$ times a function of $H$. Since $Q^{GF}$ commutes with $H$, $P\star[v.,P\star]-[v.,P\star]P\star$ is $(Q^{GF})^2$ times the commutator of two functions of $H$, which vanishes; this is $2P\star v.P\star-v.(P\star)^2-(P\star)^2v.$. The degree is that of $K_0$ minus $2$, $P\star$ having degree $-1$ and $v.$ degree $0$. (ii) $(Q^{GF})^2$ vanishes on the slots of $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $\lambda^*$, and $v.$ preserves the slots; the components of $K_0$ in $A^*\otimes A$ and $c^*\otimes c$ go to $c\otimes A|_V$ and $A|_V\otimes c$. (iii) $QQ^{GF}+Q^{GF}Q=H$ and $H\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt=e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH}$ give the first identity. With $[v.,Q]=0$ it gives

and moving $v.$ to the right by the rule of (i), the right side is $-4Q^{GF}$ times $(e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH})\frac{d}{dH}\big(H\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt\big)-H\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt\,\frac{d}{dH}(e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH})$, which vanishes because $H\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt=e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH}$. Proposition 9.19 (Graphs with one vertex $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$).

and the linearised flow of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ at $J$ is

The four terms are the vertex $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ alone, $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ joined by one edge $P$ to each leg of $W$ in turn, two legs of $W$ closed by the composite kernel, and two copies of $W$ joined by it.
Proof.

As operators, $e^{\hbar\partial_P}S^{(1)}(\Delta)e^{-\hbar\partial_P}=\sum_n\frac{\hbar^n}{n!}\mathrm{ad}_{\partial_P}^n\big(S^{(1)}(\Delta)\big)$. By Lemma [9.16](#b-01761) (iii), (iv), $\mathrm{ad}_{\partial_P}(S^{(1)}(\Delta))=P\star v.$, and by [(9.3)](#b-01757) and Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (i), $\mathrm{ad}_{\partial_P}(P\star v.)$ is $\partial$ of the composite kernel, a second-order operator with constant coefficients which commutes with $\partial_P$; the series stops, which is [(9.4)](#b-01786). The derivation gives $\hbar(P\star v.)e^{W/\hbar}=\big((P\star v.)W\big)e^{W/\hbar}$, and the product rule of Definition [3.15](#b-00457) for the odd second-order operator gives $\partial(e^{W/\hbar})=\big(\hbar^{-1}\partial W+\tfrac12\hbar^{-2}(\partial(W^2)-2W\partial W)\big)e^{W/\hbar}$. ∎

In the setting of Proposition [9.19](#b-01784),
Q\,(P\star\,v.)+(P\star\,v.)\,Q=\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}_\varepsilon-\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}_T, \tag{9.6}
and, with $[-,QW]$ the graded commutator with the multiplication by $QW$,

Q\Big(e^{-W/\hbar}e^{\hbar\partial_P}\big(S^{(1)}(\Delta)e^{J/\hbar}\big)\Big)=\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),W\}_\varepsilon-\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),W\}_T-\hbar^{-1}e^{-W/\hbar}\Big[S^{(1)}(\Delta)+\hbar\,P\star\,v.+\tfrac{\hbar^2}2\,\partial_{2(P\star v.P\star\otimes1)K_0},\,QW\Big]e^{W/\hbar}. \tag{9.7}

The last term consists of $(P\star v.)(QW)$, $\tfrac\hbar2\,\partial(QW)$ and $\tfrac12\big(\partial((QW)W)-(\partial\,QW)W+(QW)\,\partial W\big)$, with $\partial$ the operator of the composite kernel: the graphs of [(9.5)](#b-01788) with $QW$ in place of one copy of $W$, with the signs reversed.
Proof.

The graded commutator of the derivations induced by two odd operators is induced by their anticommutator, and $Q\,P\star v.+P\star v.\,Q=(e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH})v.$ by Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (iii) and $[v.,Q]=0$; Lemma [9.16](#b-01761) (ii) gives [(9.6)](#b-01794). The operator $S^{(1)}(\Delta)+\hbar P\star v.+\tfrac{\hbar^2}2\partial$ in the bracket of [(9.7)](#b-01796) is odd, and its graded commutator with $Q$ is $\hbar\big(\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}_\varepsilon-\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}_T\big)$, by $Q\,S^{(1)}(\Delta)=0$, [(9.6)](#b-01794) and Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (iii). $Q$ is a derivation and $Qe^{W/\hbar}=\hbar^{-1}(QW)e^{W/\hbar}$, so $Q$ of $e^{-W/\hbar}$ times this operator applied to $e^{W/\hbar}$ consists of $-\hbar^{-1}(QW)$ times the linearised flow, of $e^{-W/\hbar}\hbar\big(\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}_\varepsilon-\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}_T\big)e^{W/\hbar}=\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),W\}_\varepsilon-\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),W\}_T$, and of minus $\hbar^{-1}e^{-W/\hbar}$ times the operator applied to $(QW)e^{W/\hbar}$. Proposition 9.21 (Scaling Ward identity).
For $0<\varepsilon<T\le\infty$,
(v.\otimes1+1\otimes v.)\,P(\varepsilon,T)=-4\Big(\varepsilon\frac{\partial}{\partial\varepsilon}+T\frac{\partial}{\partial T}\Big)P(\varepsilon,T), \tag{9.8}
and for every even $J$, with $\delta$ a square-zero parameter of degree $0$ and the derivatives in $\varepsilon$, $T$ acting on $P(\varepsilon,T)$,

\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),W(P(\varepsilon,T),J)\}=\partial_\delta W\big(P(\varepsilon,T),J+\delta\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),J\}\big)+4\Big(\varepsilon\frac{\partial}{\partial\varepsilon}+T\frac{\partial}{\partial T}\Big)W\big(P(\varepsilon,T),J\big). \tag{9.9}

By Proposition [7.10](#b-01286), $(v.\otimes1+1\otimes v.)L_t=-4L_t-4t\frac{d}{dt}L_t$; integration over $(\varepsilon,T)$ gives $-4[tL_t]_\varepsilon^T=4\varepsilon L_\varepsilon-4TL_T$, and $\partial_\varepsilon P(\varepsilon,T)=-L_\varepsilon$, $\partial_TP(\varepsilon,T)=L_T$. By [(9.3)](#b-01757) with $X=v.$, $v.\,\partial_P=\partial_P\,v.-\partial_{(v.\otimes1+1\otimes v.)P}$, and the operators $\partial_\phi$ commute, so $v.\,e^{\hbar\partial_P}=e^{\hbar\partial_P}v.+4\big(\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon+T\partial_T\big)e^{\hbar\partial_P}$. Apply this to $e^{J/\hbar}$, use $v.\,e^{J/\hbar}=\hbar^{-1}(v.J)e^{J/\hbar}$ and Lemma [9.16](#b-01761) (i), and divide by $\hbar^{-1}e^{W/\hbar}$. ∎

At $T=\infty$ this is twice Theorem [6.6](#b-01105).

modulo constants and $\hbar^2$, the arity-one part along $\Delta$ of [(7.4)](#b-01373) with the finite counterterm included.

Proposition 9.29 (The composite triangle).

Let $O$ be a scalar bilinear, and consider the one-loop graph of the arity-one part of $O[\infty]$ along $\Delta$ whose cycle contains $O$, a cubic vertex of type $A|_V(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})^2$, the vertex $([A,c],A^*)$ and the composite kernel from the leg $A|_V$ of the first to the leg $c$ of the second; its external legs are $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, of momentum $p_1$, and $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, of momentum $p_2$, with $p_1+p_2+k=0$ for the momentum $k$ of $\omega$. In the form $\alpha(p_1)\delta(p_1+p_2+k)+\beta(p_1)^\mu\frac{\partial}{\partial p_2^\mu}\delta(p_1+p_2+k)$, with $p_1$ held fixed and the value of $O$ taken with the polarisation of $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ in place of its second leg, the value of the graph is $\alpha=0$ and

\beta(p_1)=8\,\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}\,(\text{value of }O)\,\Big(\frac{p_2}{|p_2|^2}+16\pi^2|p_1|^2\int\frac{d^4l}{(2\pi)^4}\,\frac{l}{|l|^4\,|l+p_2|^2\,|l-p_1|^2}\Big).

Q\,(\text{composite triangle})=-2\,\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}\,\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),O\}. \tag{9.15}
Proof.

The composite line is longitudinal, so by the Ward identity at the vertex $A|_V(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})^2$ the graph is a bubble term plus $|p_1|^2$ times the triangle vector integral, with $\alpha=0$; its two coefficients are $8$ and $8$, the values fixed by Remark [9.30](#b-01867). The term with $\frac{\partial}{\partial p_2}\delta$ carries the explicit position of the density. Exchanging the two legs turns $(\alpha,\beta)$ into $\big(\alpha(p_2)-\tfrac{\partial\beta^\mu}{\partial p_1^\mu}(p_2),\,\beta(p_2)\big)$, with $p_2=-p_1-k$, by $g(p_2)\,\partial\delta=g(-p_1-k)\,\partial\delta-(\partial g)(-p_1-k)\,\delta$, and a functional of two legs of the same field depends on its value through the sum of the value and its exchange. $Q$ replaces the leg $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ by $-\tfrac12d^*dA|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ (Proposition [1.11](#b-00135)), which multiplies the value by $-\tfrac12|p_2|^2$ and, by the same rule, turns $(0,\beta)$ into $\big((p_2,\beta),-\tfrac12|p_2|^2\beta\big)$. The vector integral is odd under the exchange of its two momenta, by $l\mapsto-l$, and its divergence in $p_1$ at fixed $k$ is $2|p_1|^{-2}|p_2|^{-2}$, by $\partial_\nu(l^\nu|l|^{-4})=2\pi^2\delta^4(l)$. In the sum over the two orderings the terms containing the integral cancel: the coefficient of $\partial\delta$ is $-4p_2-4p_1=4k$ and that of $\delta$ is $8$, in units times the value of $O$. The classical transformation $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),O\}=2(E+2)O$ has the value $-4$ and $-2k$ in the same form, by $\int\mathrm{dvol}\,e^{i(k,x)}2\big((x,\partial)+2\big)=2\int\mathrm{dvol}\,\big(-2-i(k,x)\big)e^{i(k,x)}$; the ratio is $-2$. ∎

10. The one-loop counterterms of all local operators

Chapters 5, 6 and 9 computed the one-loop counterterm and the dilatation component of the scalar bilinears graph by graph. A general local operator has letters of every slot with any number of derivatives, so its one-loop graphs form an infinite family and a graph-by-graph treatment reaches no end. At one loop, however, the cycle of a graph meets a local operator in exactly two of its letters and a tree meets it in one, so the counterterm of every local operator is a sum over pairs of letters of a universal pair kernel, and every one-loop component of Definition [8.16](#b-01496) with a local representative is a sum of a two-body and a one-body operator. This chapter computes the pair kernels in closed form, bounds their outputs by Weyl weight and degree, organises them by the BRST covariance of the logarithmic coefficient, evaluates them at the lowest weight and on the planar sectors whose spectrum is that of Beisert's one-loop dilatation operator, and writes the dilatation component $D_1$ and the translation component $P_1$ as the pair kernels plus composite terms, which it evaluates on the planar scalar sector.

The unit is $\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$, equal to $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$ for $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(N)$ (Remark [6.13](#b-01157)). Edges carry $P(\varepsilon,T)$ of Definition [8.3](#b-01429); every counterterm and every component below is independent of the endpoint $T$ of the transfer, and is evaluated at $T=\infty$ where the graph sums converge (Proposition [8.25](#b-01548)). On arity zero the classical differential is $Q+\{I,-\}$, the restriction of $s$ of Theorem [8.8](#b-01457). The field-counting functional is $2\int(A,A^*)-4\int(\lambda^*,\lambda)-\int(c^*,c)$ (Chapter 6); by Lemma [6.7](#b-01121) its bracket multiplies the coordinate functionals of $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $A^*$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ by $1$, $2$, $4$, $-2$, $-4$, $-1$, and by Theorem [4.22](#b-00805) the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is the unit times $(Q+\{I,-\})$ of it. Every functional containing $\lambda$ or $\lambda^*$, and every main formula, is given in the two-component form of Definition [8.1](#b-01405) in Remark [10.50](#b-02278).
10.1 The counterterm map of a local functional
Definition 10.1 (Letters, pair weight and pair degree).

A letter is a factor $\partial^\alpha\varphi$ of a monomial of the density of a local functional (Definition [5.1](#b-00894)): $\varphi$ is a coordinate functional of one slot of $\mathscr E$ (Definition [3.10](#b-00427)), the component of $c$, $A|_V$, $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$, $A^*$, $\lambda^*$ or $c^*$ along an element of its fibre, and $\partial^\alpha$ is a product of $|\alpha|$ derivatives along $V$. The Weyl weight $w_{\partial^\alpha\varphi}$ of the letter is the Weyl weight of its slot (Definition [6.1](#b-01067)) plus $|\alpha|$, and its degree is the degree of $\varphi$: $+1$, $0$, $0$, $-1$, $-1$, $-2$ for $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $A^*$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ (proof of Lemma [9.2](#b-01650)). A monomial local functional is
M=\int\omega\,X_1X_2\cdots X_n,

with letters $X_1,\dots,X_n$ at one point, $\omega\in\Omega^4_c(\mathbb R^4)$, or $\omega=\mathrm{dvol}$ for a translation-invariant $M$, and the fibre and colour factors of the letters contracted with constant tensors. For two letters $X_a$, $X_b$ the pair weight is $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$ and the pair degree is the sum of their degrees. The single letters of Proposition [5.11](#b-00986) are the monomials with one letter.

For a homogeneous local functional $M$ of degree $|M|$ and a square-zero parameter $\delta$ of degree $-|M|$ [CG2, Def 8.3.1.1], $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$ is the $\delta$-component of the one-loop counterterm of the family $I+\delta M$ (Proposition [5.3](#b-00907), Definition [8.11](#b-01473)):
\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)=\hbar\sum_\gamma\frac1{|\operatorname{Aut}\gamma|}\,\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon\,w_\gamma(\varepsilon), \tag{10.1}

the sum over the connected one-particle-irreducible graphs $\gamma$ with $b_1(\gamma)=1$ whose cycle contains the vertex $M$, all other vertices labelled by $I$ and every edge by $P(\varepsilon,T)$, with $\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon$ of Definition [4.1](#b-00556). With $I_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}$ in place of $I$ the same construction gives the counterterm of a local cochain (Definition [8.5](#b-01442)), whose arity-zero part is [(10.1)](#b-01918).
Proposition 10.2 (Structure of the counterterm map).
For a homogeneous local functional $M$ of Weyl weight $w_M$:

• (i) $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$ is a combination of $\varepsilon^{-m}$, $1\le m\le\tfrac12w_M$, and $\log\varepsilon$, with local coefficients; at one loop no power of $\log\varepsilon$ beyond the first and no product $\varepsilon^{-m}\log\varepsilon$ occurs.
• (ii) The coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ is local of Weyl weight $w_M-2m$, the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ is local of Weyl weight $w_M$, and $\omega$ is untouched.

• (iii) The singular part of every graph of [(10.1)](#b-01918) is the same for every $T\in(0,\infty]$; at $T<\infty$ it is defined at every configuration of the leg momenta, at $T=\infty$ at generic ones. Hence $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$ is independent of $T$.

• (iv) $M\mapsto\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$ is linear, linear in $\omega$, preserves the degree and the parity, and is covariant under translations, $\mathrm{Spin}(4,\mathbb C)\times\mathrm{Spin}(6,\mathbb C)$ and the adjoint action of $\mathfrak g$.
• (v) With $v=2E$ and $v.$ of Lemma [9.16](#b-01761) (i), $v.M=2(E+w_M)M$ for $M=\int\omega\,(\cdots)$,

\Big(v.-4\varepsilon\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\Big)\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)=\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](v.M)-4\big(\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)\big). \tag{10.2}
Proof.

(i), (ii). By Lemma [4.6](#b-00594) each graph is $\sum_{1\le k\le D/2}\varepsilon^{-k}a_k+b\log\varepsilon$ plus a function with a limit, $D$ its superficial degree. In the Schwinger form the singular terms come from the integral of $\tau^{-1-k}$, $k\ge1$, or of $\tau^{-1}$ over the total Schwinger time $\tau\in[\varepsilon/\min_e\alpha_e,1]$ (Theorem [10.22](#b-02082)), which produces $\varepsilon^{-k}$ and $\log\varepsilon$ alone. By Lemma [10.11](#b-01994), $D$ is the pair weight of the two letters of $M$ on the cycle minus the Weyl weight of the outputs, so the coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ has momentum degree $D-2m$ and output weight equal to the pair weight minus $2m$, and the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ has output weight equal to the pair weight; the other letters are untouched (Theorem [10.4](#b-01942)). The output weight is nonnegative, so $m$ is at most half the pair weight, which is at most $\tfrac12w_M$.

(iii). With edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$ the Schwinger times run over $[\varepsilon,T]^{E(\gamma)}$. For $\tau_0<\min(T,1)$, on $\{\tau\le\tau_0\}$ the domain is independent of $T$ and the proof of Lemma [4.6](#b-00594) gives all terms $\varepsilon^{-k}$ and $\log\varepsilon$. On $\{\tau\ge\tau_0\}$ the integrand after the Gaussian loop integral is bounded by a multiple of $\tau^{-2-j}$; at $T<\infty$ the domain is compact in $\tau$, and at $T=\infty$ the factor $e^{-\tau\cdot(\text{momentum form})}$ of Definition [10.21](#b-02076), the momentum form being at least $\tfrac12\min_{e\ne f}|q_e-q_f|^2(1-\max_e\alpha_e)$, gives convergence at generic momenta. This part has a limit by dominated convergence, and its $\varepsilon\frac d{d\varepsilon}$, the faces $t_e=\varepsilon$ of Proposition [4.2](#b-00561), is $O(\varepsilon)$. This is Proposition [8.6](#b-01448) (i) for the vertex $M$.

(iv). The vertex functions and $P(\varepsilon,T)$ are translation invariant and covariant (proof of Theorem [4.16](#b-00707)); the singular part is a polynomial in the leg momenta times the Fourier transform of $\omega$ at minus the total momentum. Every vertex and every component of $P(\varepsilon,T)$ has degree $0$ and is even.

(v). By Lemma [6.4](#b-01092), $(\sigma_sM)^{CT}[s^2\varepsilon]=\sigma_s\big(\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)\big)+2\log s\,\sigma_s\big(\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\big)$. Apply $s\frac d{ds}\big|_{s=1}$, use $2s\frac d{ds}\big|_{s=1}\sigma_s=v.$ on functionals (proof of Corollary [9.22](#b-01807)) and multiply by $2$:

\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](v.M)+4\varepsilon\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)=v.\,\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)+4\big(\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)\big).
10.2 Two letters on the cycle
Definition 10.3 (The dressed propagator and the pair kernel).

Let $e$ be a field configuration, compactly supported, with its odd components multiplied by odd elements of an auxiliary nilpotent ring (Definition [1.13](#b-00162)), and let $P=P(\varepsilon,T)$. The dressed propagator at $e$ is the kernel
\sum_{k\ge0}\Big(\big(\text{one-loop operator}\big)^kP\star\otimes1\Big)K_0,

with the one-loop operator of $P$ and of the part of $I(e+f)$ quadratic in the fluctuation $f$ (Proposition [3.23](#b-00524)) and $P\star$ the operator represented by $P$ (Definition [8.3](#b-01429)); it is a formal power series in $e$, even and graded symmetric. Its term with $k$ factors of the one-loop operator is the sum of the chains of $k$ vertices of $I$, each entered and left through two of its slots and joined by $k+1$ edges $P$, the other slots evaluated at $e$. For two letters $X_a=\partial^\alpha\varphi_a$ and $X_b=\partial^\beta\varphi_b$ the pair kernel is

\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](X_aX_b):=\hbar\,\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon\Big[\partial^\alpha_x\partial^\beta_y\Big(\text{value of }\partial_{\text{dressed propagator}}\text{ on }\varphi_a(x)\varphi_b(y)\Big)\Big]_{y=x}, \tag{10.3}

with $\partial_\phi$ of [C07, §6.4] read as in Definition [3.10](#b-00427), $\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon$ applied to each Taylor component in $e$, and $e$ then replaced by the fields. It is a local density of the fields at $x$, the outputs, with coefficients in the span of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ and $\log\varepsilon$, and with values in the tensor product of the fibres and colour spaces of the two letters, whose factors are left open; the letters of a monomial other than $X_a$, $X_b$ are its spectators.
Theorem 10.4 (Decomposition).
Let $M=\int\omega\,X_1X_2\cdots X_n$ be a monomial local functional.

• (i) The order-$\hbar$, $\delta$-linear part of $W\big(P(\varepsilon,T),I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]+\delta M(\varepsilon)\big)$ is the sum of (A) the graphs whose cycle passes through $M$, (B) the graphs with $M$ on a tree and a cycle of vertices of $I$, (C) the trees with one vertex $-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ and one vertex $M$, and (D) the trees with one vertex $-\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$. A cycle passes through $M$ along exactly two of its half-edges, two letters $X_a$, $X_b$ with $a\ne b$, and the graphs (A) are the trees of $I$ attached to the legs of $\hbar\,\partial_{\text{dressed propagator}}M$, evaluated at the legs.

• (ii) (B)$+$(C) has a limit as $\varepsilon\to0$, at generic leg momenta for $T=\infty$ and at all leg momenta for $T<\infty$; the graphs with $M$ on a tree contribute nothing to $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$.
• (iii) With the Koszul sign $(-1)^{|X_b|(|X_{a+1}|+\cdots+|X_{b-1}|)}$ of moving $X_b$ next to $X_a$, $|\cdot|$ the total parity, and $\widehat{X_b}$ omitted,

\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)=\sum_{1\le a<b\le n}(-1)^{|X_b|(|X_{a+1}|+\cdots+|X_{b-1}|)}\int\omega\,X_1\cdots X_{a-1}\,\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](X_aX_b)\,X_{a+1}\cdots\widehat{X_b}\cdots X_n : \tag{10.4}

a sum over the unordered pairs of letters of the pair kernel times the spectators, without one-body terms. For $n=2$, $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](\int\omega\,X_aX_b)=\int\omega\,\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](X_aX_b)$.

• (iv) The term $k=0$ of the pair kernel, $\hbar\,\partial^\alpha_x\partial^\beta_y$ of the component of $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ in the slots of $\varphi_a$, $\varphi_b$ at $y=x$, is a pure power $\varepsilon^{-(w_{X_a}+w_{X_b})/2}$ times a number (Lemma [10.6](#b-01963)): it has no $\log\varepsilon$ and no finite part.
Proof.

(i) By Proposition [3.22](#b-00513) at order $\hbar$, the $\delta$-linear part consists of the connected graphs with one vertex $M$ and either one cycle and vertices $I$, or no cycle and one vertex of $-\hbar^{-1}I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ or of $-\hbar^{-1}\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$: these are (A)–(D). A cycle passes through a vertex along two half-edges, which for $M$ are two letters. For (A), by Lemma [4.7](#b-00615) the graph is a tree whose vertex $s$ is labelled by the one-particle-irreducible cycle through $M$; the sum over these cycles is the $\delta$-linear part of [(3.5)](#b-00526) for the family $I+\delta M$ at the configuration $e$ of the half-edges of $s$. With the one-loop operators of $I$ and of $\delta M$ at $e$, $\tfrac\hbar2\sum_{n\ge1}\frac1n\mathrm{STr}\big((\text{one-loop operator of }I+\text{one-loop operator of }\delta M)^n\big)$ has the $\delta$-linear part
\frac\hbar2\,\mathrm{STr}\Big(\big(\text{one-loop operator of }\delta M\big)\big(1-\text{one-loop operator of }I\big)^{-1}\Big),

by cyclicity of the supertrace for even operators. By the first identity in the proof of Proposition [3.23](#b-00524), $\tfrac12\mathrm{STr}$ of the one-loop operator of a quadratic functional with an even graded-symmetric kernel $\phi$ is $\partial_\phi$ of the functional; here $\phi$ is the dressed propagator and the quadratic functional is the part of $\delta M$ quadratic in the fluctuation at $e$. Hence the cycles through $M$ sum to $\delta\,\hbar\,\partial_{\text{dressed propagator}}M$ at $e$, the operator $\partial$ being even.

(ii) For (B), removing the edge that joins the cycle to the part containing $M$ leaves a one-particle-irreducible cycle $\gamma'$ of vertices $I$ (Lemma [4.7](#b-00615)); the trees (C) with $-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ in place of $\gamma'$ remove its singular part (Definition [4.1](#b-00556)). At generic leg momenta every edge of the trees carries a nonzero momentum and two distinct edges of $\gamma'$ carry different momenta: $M$ carries the Fourier transform of $\omega$ at minus the total momentum of its legs, momentum is conserved at every other vertex, an edge of a tree separates a part without $M$ that carries a leg, and for two edges of $\gamma'$ the arc between them that avoids the half-edge to $M$ contains a vertex, the difference of the two momenta being the sum of the leg momenta entering along this arc. Then Lemma [4.6](#b-00594) applies to $\gamma'$ minus its singular part, and the tree edges converge to $P(0,\infty)$ at nonzero momentum (Proposition [4.8](#b-00628)). Cycles $\gamma'$ with one half-edge vanish (Lemma [4.7](#b-00615)). At $T<\infty$ no genericity is needed (Proposition [10.2](#b-01920) (iii)).

(iii) (A)$+$(D) has a limit exactly when (D) removes the singular part of the vertex $s$ (Lemma [4.6](#b-00594), Proposition [5.3](#b-00907)), which is local; by (i) and the uniqueness of the counterterm, $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)=\hbar\,\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon\,\partial_{\text{dressed propagator}}M$ with $e$ replaced by the fields. The operator $\partial_\phi=\tfrac12\sum\partial_{\phi''}\partial_{\phi'}$ is of order two: on $X_1\cdots X_n$ it is the sum over the pairs $a<b$ of the term in which $X_b$ is brought next to $X_a$ by Koszul reordering and the adjacent pair is replaced by the component of $\phi$ in the same order (edge rule of Proposition [3.22](#b-00513)), the derivatives of the two letters acting on the two arguments. Each Taylor component in $e$ is a finite sum of cycles, which is [(10.3)](#b-01940).
Lemma 10.5 (Sign of the pair kernels).

The pair kernel is $\hbar\,\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon$ of the value of $\partial_{\text{dressed propagator}}$ on $X_a(x)X_b(y)$ at $y=x$, read with the first factor in the slot of $X_a$ and the Koszul signs of the vertices of $I$ in the order of the chain from $X_a$ to $X_b$. In the second-derivative form of Proposition [3.23](#b-00524), with the second left derivative of $M$ in place of that of $\delta M$,
\partial_j\partial_l(\delta M)=(-1)^{|M|(|j|+|l|)}\,\delta\,\partial_j\partial_lM,

so that for $M=\int\omega\,X_aX_b$ the supertrace value with the second derivative of $M$ is $(-1)^{|X_a|+|X_b|}$ times the pair kernel; this sign differs from $1$ exactly for the pairs with one odd letter.
Proof.

The first statement is [(10.3)](#b-01940) with the edge rule of Proposition [3.22](#b-00513). For the second, $\delta$, of the parity of $M$, is moved to the left through the two left derivatives; for $M=\int\omega\,X_aX_b$ the derivatives hit the slots of $X_a$ and $X_b$, so $|j|+|l|=|X_a|+|X_b|=|M|$ and $(-1)^{|M|^2}=(-1)^{|X_a|+|X_b|}$. ∎
Lemma 10.6 (The self-contraction).
The scalar factor of $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ (Proposition [3.11](#b-00430)) has the Taylor series
\frac{1-e^{-|x|^2/4\varepsilon}}{4\pi^2|x|^2}=\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{16\pi^2\,m!\,\varepsilon^m}\Big(\frac{|x|^2}4\Big)^{m-1}.
For a multi-index $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|=2(m-1)$ its derivative $\partial^\gamma$ at $x=0$ is
\frac{(-1)^{m+1}}{16\pi^2\,m\,2^{m-1}\,\varepsilon^m}\sum_{\text{pairings of the indices of }\gamma}\ \prod\delta ,

and it vanishes for $|\gamma|$ odd. Every component of $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$ is a constant-coefficient differential operator of order $w_1+w_2-2$, $w_1$, $w_2$ the Weyl weights of its two slots, applied to the scalar factor, times its fibre factor: $2(-,-)^{-1}\otimes(\text{inverse metric of }V_{10})$ for $A\otimes A$, $-(-,-)^{-1}d$ for $c\otimes A^*|_V$, and the Dirac operator on $\lambda\otimes\lambda$. With $\partial^\alpha_x\partial^\beta_yf(x-y)|_{y=x}=(-1)^{|\beta|}(\partial^{\alpha+\beta}f)(0)$, the term $k=0$ of $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](\partial^\alpha\varphi_a\,\partial^\beta\varphi_b)$ is $(-1)^{|\beta|}\hbar$ times the fibre factor times $\partial^{\alpha+\beta}$ of that operator applied to the scalar factor at $0$: a single power $\varepsilon^{-(w_{X_a}+w_{X_b})/2}$, zero when $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$ is odd. At $T<\infty$ the additional term $-\frac{1-e^{-|x|^2/4T}}{4\pi^2|x|^2}$ of the scalar factor (Definition [8.3](#b-01429)) is regular in $\varepsilon$.
Proof.

$1-e^{-z}=\sum_{m\ge1}(-1)^{m+1}z^m/m!$ with $z=|x|^2/4\varepsilon$ gives the series. For $|\gamma|=2(m-1)$, $\partial^\gamma(|x|^2)^{m-1}$ at $0$ is $2^{m-1}(m-1)!$ times the sum over the pairings of the indices of $\gamma$ of the products of Kronecker deltas, and $\frac{(m-1)!\,2^{m-1}}{4^{m-1}m!}=\frac1{m\,2^{m-1}}$. The scalar factor is entire in $|x|^2$, so each Taylor coefficient is a single power of $\varepsilon$, and the total order of differentiation $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-2$ fixes $m=\tfrac12(w_{X_a}+w_{X_b})$. ∎
Example 10.7 (The vacuum term of the scalar bilinears).

For $M=\int\omega\,(\iota_{w_1}A,\iota_{w_2}A)$ the term $k=0$ gives $\frac{2\hbar\dim\mathfrak g\,(w_1,w_2)}{16\pi^2\varepsilon}\int\omega$, the graph (a) of Proposition [5.14](#b-01009): the $A\otimes A$ component at $x=0$ is $2(-,-)^{-1}\otimes(\text{inverse metric})$ times $\frac1{16\pi^2\varepsilon}$, and $(-,-)$ evaluated on $(-,-)^{-1}$ is $\dim\mathfrak g$ (Lemma [5.7](#b-00935)).
Lemma 10.8 (Colour structure of the pair kernels).
Number the output fields of a chain from $X_a$ to $X_b$ as $Y_1,\dots,Y_r$, $Y_1$ at the vertex nearest $X_a$, and write $Y_j$ also for the colour factor of the $j$-th output.

• (i) For a simple $\mathfrak g$, the factor in the colour spaces of the two letters of every Taylor component of the dressed propagator is a combination of the elements $(1\otimes\mathrm{ad}_{Y_r}\cdots\mathrm{ad}_{Y_1})(-,-)^{-1}$, with factors $\mathrm{ad}_{[Y_j,Y_{j+1}]}$ from quartic vertices, the first factor in the colour slot of $X_a$; $r=0$ for $k=0$.

• (ii) Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{gl}(N)$ or $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $(X,Y)=\kappa\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ with a constant $\kappa$, so that $(-,-)^{-1}=\kappa^{-1}\sum_AT_A\otimes T^A$ for dual bases, and for bosonic outputs expand
\mathrm{ad}_{Y_r}\cdots\mathrm{ad}_{Y_1}(Z)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\dots,r\}}(-1)^{r-|S|}\Big(\prod_{j\in S}^{\leftarrow}Y_j\Big)\,Z\,\Big(\prod_{j\notin S}^{\rightarrow}Y_j\Big),

the first product in decreasing and the second in increasing order of $j$. Replacing the colour factors of $X_a\otimes X_b$ by $(1\otimes\mathrm{ad}_{Y_r}\cdots\mathrm{ad}_{Y_1})(-,-)^{-1}$ maps, for products $M_1$, $M_2$ of the other colour factors (for $\mathfrak{gl}(N)$, and for $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ when $r\ge1$),

The pair $(X_1,X_n)$ of $\operatorname{tr}(X_1X_2\cdots X_n)$ is the second case with $M_1=1$, $M_2=X_2\cdots X_{n-1}$, and its leading term is $+\kappa^{-1}N\operatorname{tr}(X_2\cdots X_{n-1}Y_r\cdots Y_1)$, the first case read from $X_b$. For $r=0$ and $\mathfrak{su}(N)$: $\operatorname{tr}(M_1X_aX_b)\mapsto\kappa^{-1}(N-\tfrac1N)\operatorname{tr}M_1$, $\operatorname{tr}(M_1X_aM_2X_b)\mapsto\kappa^{-1}\big(\operatorname{tr}M_1\operatorname{tr}M_2-\tfrac1N\operatorname{tr}(M_1M_2)\big)$ and $\operatorname{tr}(M_1X_a)\operatorname{tr}(M_2X_b)\mapsto\kappa^{-1}\big(\operatorname{tr}(M_1M_2)-\tfrac1N\operatorname{tr}M_1\operatorname{tr}M_2\big)$.

• (iii) For odd letters and outputs the same formulas hold with the graded commutator $[Y,Z]=YZ-(-1)^{|Y||Z|}ZY$ in the expansion, the Koszul sign of [(10.4)](#b-01947) for the letters, and $\operatorname{tr}(ZM)=(-1)^{|Z||M|}\operatorname{tr}(MZ)$ for cyclic moves.

• (iv) For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)=2N\operatorname{tr}(XY)$, so $\frac{\hbar N}{16\pi^2\kappa}$ is half the unit: a term of the pair kernel equal to $a\,\frac{\hbar}{16\pi^2}$ times $(1\otimes\mathrm{ad}_{Y_r}\cdots\mathrm{ad}_{Y_1})(-,-)^{-1}$, $r\ge1$, contributes to an adjacent pair of a single trace $(-1)^r\tfrac a2$ units times the single trace with the pair replaced by $Y_1\cdots Y_r$, plus terms with more traces or lower powers of $N$.
Proof.

(i) Every component of $P$ has the colour factor $(-,-)^{-1}$. A cubic vertex has the colour form $(Z_1,[Z_2,Z_3])$ (Definition [1.13](#b-00162)); with output $Y$ and cycle slots $Z_2$, $Z_3$ it is $(\mathrm{ad}_YZ_2,Z_3)$, and the quartic vertex [(5.2)](#b-00948) gives $\pm(Z,\mathrm{ad}_Y\mathrm{ad}_{Y'}Z')$ or $\pm(Z,\mathrm{ad}_{[Y,Y']}Z')$. Composing along the chain from $X_a$, the vertex nearest $X_a$ acts first, and the invariance of $(-,-)$ moves the word to either factor. (ii) $[Y_r,[\cdots[Y_1,Z]]]$ expands into the sum over $S$, $Y_j$ multiplying from the left for $j\in S$ and from the right with a sign otherwise. With $\sum_A(T_A)_{ij}(T^A)_{kl}=\delta_{il}\delta_{jk}$ for $\mathfrak{gl}(N)$, $\sum_A\operatorname{tr}(PT_AQT^A)=\operatorname{tr}P\operatorname{tr}Q$ and $\sum_A\operatorname{tr}(PT_A)\operatorname{tr}(QT^A)=\operatorname{tr}(PQ)$, which give the three rules; in the first rule $S=\emptyset$ gives $\operatorname{tr}1=N$, and for the pair $(X_1,X_n)$ the complement of $S$ empty gives $\operatorname{tr}1$ and $\operatorname{tr}(M_2Y_r\cdots Y_1)$ with the sign $+1$. For $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ the completeness relation acquires $-\tfrac1N1\otimes1$, which drops out for $r\ge1$ because the word annihilates $1$. (iii) Koszul rule. (iv) The unit is $\frac{2N\hbar}{16\pi^2\kappa}$. ∎
10.3 Census of the cycles and the output bound

The components of $\lambda$ in $S_+\otimes W$ and $S_-\otimes W^*$ are written $\lambda|_{S_+\otimes W}$ and $\lambda|_{S_-\otimes W^*}$, those of $\lambda^*$ in $S_+\otimes W^*$ and $S_-\otimes W$ are written $\lambda^*|_{S_+\otimes W^*}$ and $\lambda^*|_{S_-\otimes W}$ (Proposition [1.2](#b-00068)).
Lemma 10.9 (Active letters).

A letter of $M$ on the cycle of a graph of [(10.1)](#b-01918) lies in a slot with a nonzero component of $P(\varepsilon,T)$: the active slots are $A|_V$, $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$ of both chiralities, $c$ and $A^*|_V$, and the letters of $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$ and $c^*$ are spectators of every pair kernel. The cycle leaves an active letter along one of the edges
A|_V-A|_V,\qquad A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}-A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\qquad \lambda|_{S_+\otimes W}-\lambda|_{S_-\otimes W^*},\qquad c-A^*|_V .
Proof.

A half-edge of $M$ on the cycle is contracted with a component of $P(\varepsilon,T)$ (Proposition [3.11](#b-00430)), and $\rho(p)$ exchanges the four-dimensional chiralities (Proposition [1.2](#b-00068)). ∎
Definition 10.10 (Chains).

A chain from an active letter $X_a$ to an active letter $X_b$ is a sequence of $k\ge0$ vertices of $I$, each with an entry slot and an exit slot, such that the edge of Lemma [10.9](#b-01987) leaving the slot of $X_a$ ends at the entry slot of the first vertex, consecutive vertices are joined by nonzero components of $P(\varepsilon,T)$, and the exit slot of the last vertex is joined to the slot of $X_b$; for $k=0$ the two slots are joined directly. The remaining slots of the vertices are the outputs, and their fields, read off in the order of the chain, form the leg set of the chain. The chains are the Taylor components of the dressed propagator of Definition [10.3](#b-01936); a chain and its reverse are the same cycle.
Lemma 10.11 (Superficial degree).
A cycle with edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$ through the letters $X_a$, $X_b$, whose outputs have total Weyl weight $w$ (fields only), has superficial degree $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-w$.
Proof.

Every vertex of $I$ has Weyl weight $4$, fields plus derivatives, and an edge between slots of Weyl weights $w_1$, $w_2$ has numerator degree $w_1+w_2-2$ (Proposition [3.11](#b-00430)). With $k$ vertices and $k+1$ edges the numerator degree is the sum over the vertices of $4$ minus the weights of their slots, plus the sum over the edges of $w_1+w_2-2$, plus the derivatives of the letters; the internal half-edges cancel, the letters appear in edges and the outputs in vertices, which gives $4k-2(k+1)+w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-w$. The superficial degree is this plus $4-2(k+1)$ (Lemma [4.6](#b-00594)). ∎
Proposition 10.12 (Output bound of the counterterm).
In the pair kernel $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](X_aX_b)$:
• (i) the coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ is local of Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-2m$ in the outputs, and the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ is local of Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$;

• (ii) a chain whose outputs have total Weyl weight $w$ contributes $\varepsilon^{-m}$ for $1\le m\le\tfrac12(w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-w)$ and $\log\varepsilon$ for $w\le w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$; for $w>w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$ it is convergent and contributes nothing to the counterterm;
• (iii) every output slot has Weyl weight plus degree at least $1$, with equality exactly for $c$ and $A$, and the outputs carry the pair degree, so the number of output fields is at most
w+(\text{degree of }X_a)+(\text{degree of }X_b)\ \le\ w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}+(\text{degree of }X_a)+(\text{degree of }X_b),
and the number $k$ of vertices of the chain is at most the number of output fields;
• (iv) for each pair of slots and each pair weight finitely many leg sets occur; their numbers for pair weights up to $7$ are in Table [10.2](#b-02017).
Proof.

(i), (ii): Lemma [10.11](#b-01994) and Lemma [4.6](#b-00594): the coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ has momentum degree equal to the superficial degree minus $2m$, the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ momentum degree equal to the superficial degree, the output weight is $w$ plus the momentum degree, and both coefficients vanish for negative superficial degree. (iii): the Weyl weight plus the degree is $1,1,\tfrac32,2,\tfrac32,2$ for $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $A^*$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$; vertices and edges have degree $0$, so the degrees of the outputs sum to the pair degree; each vertex has at least three slots, two of them on the cycle. (iv): finitely many leg sets satisfy (iii) at a given pair weight. ∎
Proposition 10.13 (Census).
• (i) Every chain conserves the degree, the fermion parity and the action of the centre $\mathbb Z/4$ of $SL(4,\mathbb C)$, $W\mapsto iW$.

• (ii) At the pair weight without derivatives the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ of the pair kernel has its outputs in the leg sets of Table [10.1](#b-02015), and the coefficient of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ in the leg sets of its last column; the empty leg set, the term $k=0$, enters for even pair weight only, at $m$ equal to half the pair weight.

• (iii) $k=0$ occurs exactly for the pairs $(A|_V,A|_V)$, $(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$, $(\lambda|_{S_+\otimes W},\lambda|_{S_-\otimes W^*})$ and $(c,A^*|_V)$; $k=1$ occurs for all pairs except $(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},c)$, $(\lambda,c)$ and $(c,c)$, whose shortest chains have $k=2$.

• (iv) The coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ of $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ vanishes on the leg set $A|_V$, and its two chains with the leg set $A|_V\,A|_V$, the triangle and the quartic bubble, cancel.
Proof.

(i) Each vertex of $I$ and each component of $P(\varepsilon,T)$ conserves these charges. 10.4 Covariance: the BRST relations of the pair kernels
Lemma 10.15 (Derivation rule).
For an odd derivation $d$ of the product of functionals with $d\Delta_0+\Delta_0d=0$, in particular $d=Q$, $\{I,-\}$ and $Q+\{I,-\}$,
d\{f,g\}=-\{df,g\}-(-1)^{|f|}\{f,dg\},\qquad\text{that is}\qquad [d,\{f,-\}]=-\{df,-\}.
Proof.

Insert $\{f,g\}=\Delta_0(fg)-(\Delta_0f)g-(-1)^{|f|}f\Delta_0g$ (Definition [1.6](#b-00095)) and $d(fg)=(df)g+(-1)^{|f|}f\,dg$, and move $d$ through $\Delta_0$. For $Q$, $[\partial_{K_0},Q]=\partial_{(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)K_0}=0$ (Proposition [1.11](#b-00135)); $\{I,-\}$ is a derivation anticommuting with $\Delta_0$ since $\Delta_0I=0$ (proof of Theorem [4.30](#b-00858)). For odd $f$ the identity reads $s\{f,g\}-\{f,sg\}=-\{sf,g\}$, the identity of Proposition [8.19](#b-01512) (a). ∎
Theorem 10.16 (BRST covariance of the logarithmic coefficient).
For every local functional $M$,
Equivalently, the map

M\longmapsto\big(\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)\big)-\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}\Big\{2\int(A,A^*)-4\int(\lambda^*,\lambda)-\int(c^*,c),\,M\Big\}
commutes with $Q+\{I,-\}$, and for the operators of Theorem [6.11](#b-01145) twice this map, applied to $O$, is the dilatation coefficient of that theorem times $O$.
Proof.

Take $T=\infty$ and $J=I-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]+\delta M(\varepsilon)$. By Proposition [4.26](#b-00828), $Q\,W(P(\varepsilon,\infty),J)$ is the flow of the defect vertex $QJ+\tfrac12\{J,J\}_\varepsilon+\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon J$, and it has a limit as $\varepsilon\to0$ at generic momenta (Proposition [5.3](#b-00907); $Q$ multiplies the leg functions by polynomials). Its $\delta$-linear part at order $\hbar$ consists of the following graphs.

• The tree vertices $-Q\,\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)-\{I,\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)\}_\varepsilon-\{I^{CT}[\varepsilon],M\}_\varepsilon$. The bracket $\{-,-\}_\varepsilon$ is $\{-,-\}$ plus the bracket built from $K_\varepsilon-K_0=(e^{-\varepsilon H}-1)K_0$; since $\varepsilon^{-m}(e^{-\varepsilon H}-1)=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(-H)^j}{j!}\varepsilon^{j-m}$ consists of pure powers and $\log\varepsilon\,(e^{-\varepsilon H}-1)\to0$ at a generic momentum, the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ of these vertices is minus $(Q+\{I,-\})$ of the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$ minus the bracket of the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ with $M$. Their part of order $\varepsilon^0$ is the finite local vertex

-\sum_{m\ge1}\frac{(-1)^m}{m!}\Big(\big\{I,\text{coefficient of }\varepsilon^{-m}\text{ in }\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)\big\}_{H^m}+\big\{\text{coefficient of }\varepsilon^{-m}\text{ in }I^{CT}[\varepsilon],M\big\}_{H^m}\Big), \tag{10.6}
with $\{-,-\}_{H^m}$ the bracket built from $(H^m\otimes1)K_0$ in place of $K_0$; it depends on the regularisation and enters $L_1(M)$.

• The one-loop graphs with the vertex $QM+\{I,M\}_\varepsilon$, which is $(Q+\{I,-\})M$ plus the special-edge part of $\{I,M\}_\varepsilon$. The cycles through $(Q+\{I,-\})M$ have the singular part $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]\big((Q+\{I,-\})M\big)$; the graphs with this vertex on a tree pair with the trees of $-I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ and have limits (Theorem [10.4](#b-01942) (ii)). The cycles through a special edge have no $\log\varepsilon$ (Lemma [10.24](#b-02098)), and a special edge on a bridge multiplies a singular part by $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$, which gives pure powers as above.

• $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon M$: contractions through $K_\varepsilon$, whose scalar factor $(4\pi\varepsilon)^{-2}e^{-|x|^2/4\varepsilon}$ has Taylor coefficients that are single powers of $\varepsilon$; no $\log\varepsilon$.

• The $\delta$-independent defect: at order $\hbar^0$ the special edge of $\tfrac12\{I,I\}_\varepsilon$ on a cycle through $M$, without $\log\varepsilon$, or on a bridge; at order $\hbar$ the defect of the action joined to $M$ by trees, which has a limit.

The sum has a limit, so the local vertex formed by the coefficients of $\log\varepsilon$ vanishes, the tree-level flow being injective (Theorem [8.15](#b-01488) (i)); this is [(10.5)](#b-02029). By Theorem [4.22](#b-00805) the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $I^{CT}[\varepsilon]$ is the unit times $(Q+\{I,-\})$ of the field-counting functional, which is odd, and Lemma [10.15](#b-02022) gives $\{(Q+\{I,-\})F,M\}=-(Q+\{I,-\})\{F,M\}+\{F,(Q+\{I,-\})M\}$ for the field-counting functional $F$; inserted into [(10.5)](#b-02029) this is the commutation.
