Corollary 10.17 (Ward identities of the pair kernels).

• (W1) For every single letter $N=\int\omega\,(\zeta,X)$, the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]\big((Q+\{I,-\})N\big)$, the sum over the pairs of letters of the image of $X$ of their logarithmic pair kernels, equals $\{\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }I^{CT}[\varepsilon],N\}$.

• (W2) For every pair of letters, the sum of the logarithmic pair kernels of the pairs formed by one letter of the image of $X_a$ with $X_b$, the other letters of the image being spectators, plus $(-1)^{|X_a|}$ times the same sum for $X_a$ and the image of $X_b$, equals $(Q+\{I,-\})$ applied to the outputs of the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](X_aX_b)$.
(W1) and (W2) for all letters are equivalent to [(10.5)](#b-02029).
Proof.

For a single letter $N$ the pair kernels are absent, so the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](N)$ vanishes and [(10.5)](#b-02029) is (W1). For $M=\int\omega\,X_aX_b$ the pairs of the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon]\big((Q+\{I,-\})M\big)$ inside the image of $X_a$ or of $X_b$ give $\{\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }I^{CT}[\varepsilon],M\}$ by (W1), the bracket being a derivation of degree $1$, and the pairs across the two images give the left side of (W2); $(Q+\{I,-\})$ of the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](M)$ is the right side of (W2). For $n$ letters the spectators sort in the same way, by [(10.4)](#b-01947). ∎
Proposition 10.18 (The one-body identities letter by letter).

For a single letter $N$, $\{\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }I^{CT}[\varepsilon],N\}$ is the unit times $\{S,N\}=(Q+\{I,-\})N$ with every term of $S$ weighted by its multiplier under the field-counting functional:
Hence (W1) reads, with the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](QN)$ equal to $0$, $QN$ being a single letter:

• for $X=A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$, $c$: the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](\{I,N\})$ is $1$ unit times $\{I,N\}$, from the pairs $(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},c)$, $(\lambda,c)$, $(c,c)$, and $QN=0$;
• for $X=A|_V$: it is the unit times $\{I,N\}-QN$, from the pair $(A|_V,c)$, with $QN=-\int\omega\,(\zeta,dc)$;

• for $X=A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$: it is the unit times $4QN$ plus $6$, $8$, $10$ and $1$ times the brackets of $N$ with the cubic gauge term, the quartic term, $\tfrac12\int(\lambda,({\not d}_A-{\not d})\lambda)$ and $\int([A,c],A^*)$;

• for $X=A^*|_V$ the same with the multipliers $4,6,8,10,1$ and without $(dc,A^*)$, for $X=\lambda^*$ with $8,10,1$ on the terms containing $\lambda$, and for $X=c^*$ with $-1,1,1,1$ on the terms containing $c$.
Proof.

By Lemma [4.21](#b-00796) and the proof of Theorem [4.22](#b-00805), the bracket of the unit times $(Q+\{I,-\})$ of the field-counting functional with $N$ contracts the letter of $N$ with the partner slot in each term of $S$, multiplied by the weighted count of that term. $QN$ is the contraction with the free part of $S$ and $\{I,N\}$ the contraction with $I$. ∎
Proposition 10.19 (Triangularity of (W2) and the independent data).

Grade the logarithmic pair kernels by the number $r$ of output fields, and split the image of a letter into $QX$, a single letter, and $\{I,X\}$, of at least two letters. On the active letters $Q$ acts by $A|_V\mapsto-dc$ and $A^*|_V\mapsto$ a letter $A|_V$ with two derivatives (Proposition [1.11](#b-00135)), and annihilates $c$, $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ and $\lambda$. The Q-depth of an active letter is the number of applications of $Q$ that reach a letter annihilated by $Q$: $0$ for $c$, $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$, $1$ for $A|_V$ and $2$ for $A^*|_V$; that of a pair is the sum.
• (i) The part of (W2) with $r$ output fields reads

Q\big(\text{part with }r\text{ outputs of the pair }(X_a,X_b)\big)-\big(\text{part with }r\text{ outputs of }(QX_a,X_b)\big)-(-1)^{|X_a|}\big(\text{part with }r\text{ outputs of }(X_a,QX_b)\big)=(\text{source}),

with the source built from the parts with fewer than $r$ outputs: $\{I,-\}$ on their outputs, and the pair kernels of the pairs with one letter of $\{I,X_a\}$ or of $\{I,X_b\}$, the other letters of these being spectators. The pairs $(QX_a,X_b)$ and $(X_a,QX_b)$ have Q-depth one less: the system is triangular in $r$ and the Q-depth.

• (ii) For a pair of Q-depth $0$ the equation is $Q(\text{part with }r\text{ outputs})=(\text{source})$, and its homogeneous solutions are $Q$-closed in the outputs. On a leg set of field outputs, of $c$, $A|_V$, $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ and $\lambda$, $Q$ substitutes for an output $A|_V$ of momentum $p$ and polarisation $a$ the ghost with the factor $-i(p,a)$, different outputs giving different leg sets; so a $Q$-closed kernel is annihilated by $a\mapsto p$ in every leg $A|_V$, and by the exactness of the Koszul complex $(\wedge^\bullet V^\vee\otimes\mathbb C[p],\iota_p)$ in positive degree it depends on every output $A|_V$ through $p\wedge a$, that is through $dA|_V$.

• (iii) For a pair of Q-depth at least $1$ the homogeneous solutions depend on the outputs $A|_V$ through more than $dA|_V$: a homogeneous kernel of the Q-depth-$0$ pair $(\partial^\alpha c,X_b)$ enters, through the term with $QX_a$, the equation of $(\partial^\beta A|_V,X_b)$. The pair $(A|_V,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ at pair weight $2$ has on the leg set $A|_V\,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ the logarithmic kernel $-\tfrac12(a_1,b_1)(a_2,b_2)$, the sum of its two chains in Proposition [10.29](#b-02134), which depends on the output $A|_V$ through more than $dA|_V$.

• (iv) Hence the data that (W2) leaves free, given the parts with fewer outputs, are at each $r$: the $Q$-closed parts of the kernels of the pairs of Q-depth $0$, the pairs $(\partial^\alpha c,X_b)$ with derivatives of the ghost, on which (W1) fixes the combinations that enter the image of $\partial^\alpha X$, for example the sum of the pair kernels of $(\partial A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},c)$ and $(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\partial c)$, and the $Q$-closed parts of the kernels of the pairs of Q-depth at least $1$. The covariant completion of the outputs, $d\mapsto d_A$ and $dA\mapsto F_A$, is fixed by (i) from the parts with fewer outputs.
Proof.

(i) is the part of (W2) with $r$ output fields: $\{I,-\}$ on a kernel adds one or two fields; in the pair kernels of $(\{I,X_a\},X_b)$ the letters of $\{I,X_a\}$ other than the paired one are spectators, so the kernel part has fewer outputs; $QX$ is a single letter of the next lower Q-depth (Proposition [1.11](#b-00135)). (ii) For letters of Q-depth $0$, $QX_a=QX_b=0$. On field outputs, $Q$ of a functional linear in an output $A|_V$ of polarisation $a$ substitutes $a\mapsto-ip$ times the ghost; vanishing for all ghosts gives a dependence $(a,h(p))$ with $(p,h(p))=0$, and $h=\iota_pg$ with $g$ antisymmetric, so the dependence is $g(p,a)$. Antifield outputs are moved by $Q$ into other leg sets, $A^*\to A$, $\lambda^*\to\lambda$, $c^*\to A^*$, and couple the leg sets; (ii) is stated for field outputs. (iii) The kernel $-\tfrac12(a_1,b_1)(a_2,b_2)$ changes under $b_1\mapsto p_1$ to $-\tfrac12(a_1,p_1)(a_2,b_2)\neq0$. (iv) Induction on $r$ and the Q-depth with (i)–(iii). ∎

10.5 Closed forms: simplex integrals and generating functions
Definition 10.21 (Cycle data).

For a chain with $k$ vertices the cycle has $k+1$ edges $e_0,\dots,e_k$, with $e_0$ leaving $X_a$, $e_k$ ending at $X_b$ and $e_j$ joining the $j$-th to the $(j+1)$-th vertex. Let $q_j$ be the sum of the incoming momenta of the outputs of the first $j$ vertices, $q_0=0$, so that $e_j$ carries $l+q_j$ for the loop momentum $l$ and the letters have the incoming momenta $-l$ and $l+q_k$. The numerator is the polynomial in $l$ and the output momenta formed by the vertex functions, the polynomial factors of the edges, the fibre elements and the colour factors (Lemma [4.6](#b-00594)); the chain numerator is the numerator without the factors of the two letters. On the simplex $\{\alpha\in[0,1]^{k+1}:\sum_j\alpha_j=1\}$, with the Lebesgue measure $d\alpha$ of $(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k)$, the centre of the cycle is $-\sum_j\alpha_jq_j$ and its momentum form is
\sum_j\alpha_j|q_j|^2-\Big|\sum_j\alpha_jq_j\Big|^2=\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i\alpha_j|q_i-q_j|^2 .
For $m\ge0$ the $m$-th simplex integrand is
\sum_{j\ge m+k-1}\frac{\big((\textstyle\sum_\mu\partial^2_{l_\mu})^j\,\text{numerator}\big)(\text{centre})}{j!\,4^j}\;\frac{(-\text{momentum form})^{\,j+1-k-m}}{(j+1-k-m)!},
a polynomial in $\alpha$ and the output momenta. For each edge $e$ the region of the simplex where $\alpha_e$ is the smallest of the $\alpha$'s has volume $\frac1{k+1}$ of the simplex.
Theorem 10.22 (Singular coefficients as simplex integrals).
The value of the cycle with edges $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$,
\int_{[\varepsilon,\infty)^{k+1}}\prod_jdt_j\int\frac{d^4l}{(2\pi)^4}\,(\text{numerator})\,\prod_je^{-t_j|l+q_j|^2},
has, at generic output momenta, the coefficients

The first integral is the sum over the edges $e$ of the integrals of $\alpha_e^m$ times the integrand over the region where $\alpha_e$ is the smallest, the graph with $e$ labelled by $-\varepsilon L_\varepsilon$ of Proposition [4.2](#b-00561). Every coefficient is a polynomial in the output momenta with rational coefficients, by $\int\prod_e\alpha_e^{n_e}\,d\alpha=\prod_en_e!/(\sum_en_e+k)!$; every coefficient of a pair kernel is a rational multiple of $\frac{\hbar}{16\pi^2}$ times its colour and fibre factors.
Proof.
$\sum_jt_j|l+q_j|^2=\tau|l-\text{centre}|^2+\tau\cdot(\text{momentum form})$ with $\tau=\sum_jt_j$ and $\alpha_j=t_j/\tau$. The Gaussian integral (Lemma [4.4](#b-00577), iterated) is
\int\frac{d^4l}{(2\pi)^4}\,(\text{numerator})\,e^{-\tau|l-\text{centre}|^2}=\frac1{16\pi^2\tau^2}\sum_j\frac{\big((\sum_\mu\partial^2_{l_\mu})^j\,\text{numerator}\big)(\text{centre})}{j!\,(4\tau)^j}.

With $\prod_jdt_j=\tau^kd\tau\,d\alpha$ and the cutoff $\tau\ge\varepsilon/\min_e\alpha_e$, the expansion of $e^{-\tau\cdot(\text{momentum form})}$ gives powers $\tau^{-1-n}$, and $\int_{\varepsilon/\min_e\alpha_e}^1\tau^{-1-n}d\tau$ is $\frac1n\big(\varepsilon^{-n}(\min_e\alpha_e)^n-1\big)$ for $n\ge1$ and $-\log\varepsilon+\log\min_e\alpha_e$ for $n=0$; the region $\tau\ge1$ has a limit. Proposition 10.23 (Shape independence of the logarithm).

For a Schwinger domain $\{\tau\ge\varepsilon\cdot(\text{cutoff shape})\}$, the cutoff shape a positive function on the interior of the simplex with integrable logarithm ($1/\min_e\alpha_e$ for the cutoff on every edge, $1$ for a cutoff on the total Schwinger time),

$\int_{\varepsilon\cdot\text{shape}}^1\tau^{-1-n}d\tau$ is $\frac1n\big((\varepsilon\cdot\text{shape})^{-n}-1\big)$ for $n\ge1$ and $-\log\varepsilon-\log(\text{shape})$ for $n=0$; the other regions have limits independent of the shape. The examples are exact evaluations of these integrals. ∎

10.7 Planar densities and spectra

Throughout this section $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(N)$ at leading order in $N$, $O$ is a single trace of letters, every adjacent pair of the trace, the pair of the last and the first letter included, receives the leading term of Lemma [10.8](#b-01973) (ii), and the bracket with the unit times the field-counting functional is distributed over the adjacent pairs, half of the weight of each letter to each of its two pairs. The map

O\longmapsto\big(\text{coefficient of }\log\varepsilon\text{ in }\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](O)\big)-\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}\Big\{2\int(A,A^*)-4\int(\lambda^*,\lambda)-\int(c^*,c),\,O\Big\}
of Theorem [10.16](#b-02027) is then a sum over the adjacent pairs of a two-site density; twice it is the dilatation coefficient of Theorem [6.11](#b-01145).
Proposition 10.31 (The planar scalar density).

On single traces of letters $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ without derivatives, on the part with outputs $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ of the pair kernel of an adjacent pair acts as

\operatorname{tr}(\cdots\iota_{w_1}A\,\iota_{w_2}A\cdots)\longmapsto\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}\Big[2\operatorname{tr}(\cdots\iota_{w_2}A\,\iota_{w_1}A\cdots)-(w_1,w_2)\sum_K\operatorname{tr}(\cdots\iota_{e_K}A\,\iota_{e_K}A\cdots)\Big],
$e_K$ an orthonormal basis of $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$, and the two-site density of the map above is $-2$ units times
\operatorname{tr}(\cdots\iota_{w_1}A\,\iota_{w_2}A\cdots)-\operatorname{tr}(\cdots\iota_{w_2}A\,\iota_{w_1}A\cdots)+\tfrac12(w_1,w_2)\sum_K\operatorname{tr}(\cdots\iota_{e_K}A\,\iota_{e_K}A\cdots).
On the outputs $A|_V\,A|_V$ the two chains cancel. On the bilinears the map is $0$ on the twenty traceless ones and $-12$ units on the trace.
Proof.

(Z,\psi)\mapsto1\cdot(Z\psi)+2\cdot(\psi Z),\qquad (Z,Z)\mapsto2\cdot(ZZ),\qquad (\psi,\psi)\mapsto0,

in units, with $(Y_1Y_2)$ the single trace with the pair replaced by $Y_1Y_2$. The two-site density of the map above is $-2$ units times one minus the graded exchange, which sends $Z\psi$ to $\psi Z$, $ZZ$ to $ZZ$ and $\psi\psi$ to $-\psi\psi$.

Let $n\in V\otimes\mathbb C$ with $(n,n)=0$, let $\iota_nd_{A|_V}$ be the covariant derivative along $n$, and let $Z=\iota_wA$ with $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp\otimes\mathbb C$, $(w,w)=0$. On the families of Propositions [10.31](#b-02152)–[10.34](#b-02171), twice the map above, the dilatation coefficient of Theorem [6.11](#b-01145), has the spectrum of $\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}\sum_lH_{l,l+1}$, with the two-site Hamiltonian $H_{12}=2h(J_{12})$ of [B03c, (1.1)–(1.3)], the unit being $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$: $\frac{g^2N}{8\pi^2}$ times the spectrum of $\sum_l(1-\text{exchange}+\tfrac12\,\text{trace})$ on the scalars, of the Heisenberg Hamiltonian on the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ sector and of $\sum_l(1-\text{graded exchange})$ on the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ sector, $\frac{g^2N}{2\pi^2}h(S)$ on twist two [B03c, (2.31)], and $\frac{3g^2N}{4\pi^2}$ for the trace bilinear, the Konishi value of Remark [6.13](#b-01157). • (iii) on the part with the outputs $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ alone of the planar scalar sector the difference is $-(\tfrac13+\theta)$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ (Proposition [10.40](#b-02222)).
Proof.

Let a family of gauge-invariant cocycles stable under $\Lambda$ satisfy the hypotheses of Definition [10.36](#b-02186) for a solution $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ whose quadratic part is the translation-invariant solution of Theorem [9.25](#b-01828) (iii), and assume that on its cohomology the composite term of $O$ minus the bracket of $O$ with $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)-4$ units times the field-counting functional induces $-\tfrac13$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$. For $x$ in a homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$ let $\lambda_x$ be its $\mathrm{ad}_\Delta$ eigenvalue, as in Proposition [9.34](#b-01895): $-2$ for $P_b$, $+2$ for $K_b$, $-1$ on $\Sigma$, $+1$ on $\Sigma^*$ and $0$ for $\Delta$, $\mathfrak{so}(V)$ and $\mathfrak{so}(W_{\mathbb R}^\perp)$ (Remark [2.6](#b-00254)). Proposition 10.45 (Structure of the one-loop components).
Let $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(x)$ solve the arity-one equation along $x$, and let $O$ satisfy (ii) and (iii) of Definition [10.36](#b-02186) along $x$. Then

\hbar L_1(O)^{(1)}(x)=\sum_{a<b}\pm\int\omega\cdots\big(\text{two-body kernel of }(X_a,X_b)\text{ along }x\big)\cdots+\sum_a\int\omega\cdots\big(\text{one-body kernel of }X_a\text{ along }x\big)\cdots,

with the Koszul signs of [(10.4)](#b-01947), the two-body kernel depending on the pair and the one-body kernel on the letter alone. The two-body kernel is the $\varepsilon\to0$ limit of the local parts of the cycles through the pair that contain exactly one defect insertion, together with their images under $Q$ where the defect is read through Lemma [7.2](#b-01219): a special edge $K_\varepsilon-K_0$, from the special-edge parts of $\{I,O(\varepsilon)\}_\varepsilon$ and of $\{S^{(1)}(x),O(\varepsilon)\}_\varepsilon$; the vertex $S^{(1)}(x)$ on the cycle, which for even $x$ is the composite line of Definition [9.17](#b-01770) with the vector field of $x$ in place of $v$; or the arity-one counterterm vertex of $O$. The one-body kernel collects $-\{\hbar F_1^{(1)}(x),X\}$, the trees of the arity-zero finite counterterm with $S^{(1)}(x)$, and the defect or composite two-point functionals on one leg. For $x=\Delta$ this is Theorem [10.38](#b-02198), the scaling Ward identity adding $4$ times the logarithmic pair kernels and $-4$ units times the field-counting weights; for $x=P_b$ it is Proposition [10.42](#b-02239).
Proof.

By Lemma [8.4](#b-01435) and Definition [8.14](#b-01485) the component along $x$ of $L(O)[T]$ is read from the $\varepsilon\to0$ limit of the graphs with one defect vertex linear in $\delta$ and in $x$. At order $\hbar$ such a graph has one cycle or none; a cycle passes through $O$ along two half-edges, two letters, and a tree meets $O$ in one letter per edge. Lemma [4.7](#b-00615), as in Theorem [10.4](#b-01942) (i), separates the cycle through $O$ from the trees attached to it, which carry the fields of the outputs. The local representative and Theorem [8.15](#b-01488) (i) transfer the sum to local functionals. ∎
Lemma 10.46 (Active letters at arity one).

The special edge has the components of $K_0$: $A\otimes A^*$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda^*$, $c\otimes c^*$ and their transposes. For $x\in\Sigma$ the quadratic part of $S^{(1)}(x)$ joins $\lambda$ to $A^*$ and $A$ to $\lambda^*$ (proof of Proposition [8.25](#b-01548)), and for even $x$ it joins a field to its antifield, through $(v.A,A^*)$, $(v.\lambda,\lambda^*)$ and $(v.c,c^*)$. Hence every letter, $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$ and $c^*$ included, is active at arity one, and the cycles have edges $P(\varepsilon,T)$, at most one special edge or composite line, vertices of $I$ and at most one vertex $S^{(1)}(x)$.
Proof.
Proposition [4.27](#b-00837), the proof of Proposition [8.25](#b-01548), and Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (ii). ∎
Proposition 10.47 (Output bound along $x$).

Under (iii) of Definition [10.36](#b-02186) along $x$, the two-body kernel of $(X_a,X_b)$ along $x$ is a local functional of Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-\tfrac12\lambda_x$, the position counted at weight $-1$, a polynomial in the position of degree at most that of $x$, of the pair degree and of the fermion parity $|X_a|+|X_b|+|x|$; its number of output fields is at most
w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-\tfrac12\lambda_x+(\text{degree of }x\text{ in the position})+(\text{degree of }X_a)+(\text{degree of }X_b).
For each pair of slots and each pair weight finitely many leg sets enter.

$\{S^{(1)}(x),-\}$ shifts the Weyl weight by $-\tfrac12\lambda_x$, since $[\Delta,x]=\lambda_xx$, and preserves the degree. The defect insertions are built from $S^{(1)}(x)$, $I$, $K_0$ and $P(\varepsilon,T)$, each of which obeys the weight rule of Proposition [3.11](#b-00430) with the position at weight $-1$, and contain the position at most to the degree of the vector field or the Killing spinor of $x$. Locality and the bound Weyl weight plus degree at least $1$ for every output give the bound as in Proposition [10.39](#b-02215). ∎

On the Dirac column $(\lambda_\alpha{}^i,\bar\lambda^{\dot\alpha}{}_i)$, $\rho(v)=\gamma_W^\mu v_\mu$ gives Weinberg's form of each line, and with $A_m=-igA^a_mT^a$, $A_I=-igA^a_IT^a$, $\lambda=-\tfrac{ig}{\sqrt2}\lambda^aT^a$, $\operatorname{tr}(T^aT^b)=\tfrac12\delta^{ab}$, the unit is $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$.
Remark 10.51 (Method of computation).

Each chain is evaluated exactly: the Gaussian loop integral and the simplex formulas of Theorem [10.22](#b-02082), or the generating functions of Proposition [10.25](#b-02104), reduce it to Dirichlet integrals of polynomials over the simplex and over its regions, with the fibre algebra in explicit realisations of $V_{10}$ and $\Sigma$ over $\mathbb Q(i)$ and the colour words reduced by Lemma [10.8](#b-01973). A second evaluation expands the numerator in momentum space, fixes the Schwinger time of one edge at the boundary face of Proposition [4.2](#b-00561) and integrates the others; it gives the same entries at the pair weight without derivatives, at one derivative with at most two outputs, and at two derivatives with at most two outputs for the pairs of the letters $A|_V$ and $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$. The index-free entries of Tables [10.3](#b-02138)–[10.5](#b-02142) are the combinations of invariant structures that reproduce every component, and the spectra of Section 10.7 are exact diagonalisations. Every integral is a four-dimensional Schwinger integral with the cutoff $\varepsilon$ on every edge.
11. Composite kernels and the odd two-body kernels

Chapter 10 wrote the dilatation component $D_1$ and the translation component $P_1$ of a local operator as four times the logarithmic pair kernels, a one-body term and a composite term, the graphs in which $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ or $S^{(1)}(P_b)$ sits on the cycle as a line from a ghost leg to a gauge leg (Theorem [10.38](#b-02198), Proposition [10.42](#b-02239)), and evaluated the composite term on the planar scalar sector. On a general operator the locality of the composite term is a statement to be proved: on the letters $A|_V$, $\lambda$, $c$ the renormalised composite two-point functional contains $\log|p|^2$ of the momentum (Remark [9.26](#b-01842)). This chapter shows that $Q$ maps the composite graphs of a cocycle to cycles with one special edge, so that the composite term is a sum over the pairs of letters of a local kernel, the composite pair kernel; it computes these kernels as simplex integrals and evaluates them on twist two, on the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ sector, on the fermion and gluon $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sectors and on two mixed families. On all of them the composite pair kernels satisfy the two identities that Corollary [10.44](#b-02252) requires, and with the arity-two equation along $(\Delta,P_b)$ they fix the three sector coefficients of $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ to $-\tfrac13$ units: $D_1$ is four times the map of Theorem [10.16](#b-02027), with spectrum twice the one-loop anomalous dimensions, and $P_1$ vanishes on cohomology in the translation-covariant scheme. The last section sets up the two-body kernels of $Q_1$, $S_1$ and $K_1$ in the same scheme: their graphs and output bounds, the relations of $S_1$ to $Q_1$ and of $K_1$ to $P_1$, their renormalisation freedom and the comparison with the one-loop differential of the holomorphic twist.

The unit is $\frac{\hbar\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak g}(\mathrm{ad}_X\mathrm{ad}_Y)}{16\pi^2(X,Y)}$, equal to $-\frac{g^2N}{32\pi^2}$ for $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(N)$ (Remark [6.13](#b-01157)). Edges carry $P(\varepsilon,T)$ of Definition [8.3](#b-01429); the special edge is $K_\varepsilon-K_0=-\int_0^\varepsilon(H\otimes1)K_t\,dt$, the factor $e^{-\varepsilon|p|^2}-1$ times the components of $K_0$ (Proposition [4.27](#b-00837)). Every component below is independent of the endpoint $T\in(0,\infty]$ of the transfer (Theorem [8.15](#b-01488) (ii)) and is evaluated at $T=\infty$, where the graph sums converge at generic momenta (Proposition [8.25](#b-01548)); along $K_b$ it is taken at a finite $T$ (Definition [8.26](#b-01552)). On arity zero $s=Q+\{I,-\}$ (Theorem [8.8](#b-01457)). Letters, the pair weight, the pair degree and the Koszul signs are those of Definition [10.1](#b-01913) and [(10.4)](#b-01947). The field-counting functional is $2\int(A,A^*)-4\int(\lambda^*,\lambda)-\int(c^*,c)$, whose bracket multiplies the coordinate functionals of $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $A^*$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ by $1$, $2$, $4$, $-2$, $-4$, $-1$ (Lemma [6.7](#b-01121)), and the map of Theorem [10.16](#b-02027) is the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $\partial_\delta I^{CT}[\varepsilon](O)$ minus the unit times the bracket of $O$ with it (Section 10.7). Along $\Delta$, $v=2E$ and $v.$ is the operator of Lemma [9.16](#b-01761), so that $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),M\}=v.M$; along $P_b$, $v.$ is $\partial_b$ on every slot (Proposition [7.6](#b-01244)); for $x\in\{\Delta,P_b\}$, $v_x.$ is the operator of the vector field of $x$ (Definition [7.4](#b-01226)). The two-component form of Definition [8.1](#b-01405) of every main formula is in Remark [11.45](#b-02594).
11.1 The composite term as a sum over pairs
Definition 11.1 (Square kernel and composite kernels).
For $0<\varepsilon<T\le\infty$ and $P=P(\varepsilon,T)$, the square kernel is $\big((P\star)^2\otimes1\big)K_0$, and the composite kernel along $x\in\{\Delta,P_b\}$ is
\big(P\star\,v_x.\otimes1+1\otimes P\star\,v_x.\big)P,
the two legs of $S^{(1)}(x)$ joined, in both orders, to two edges $P$ (Definition [9.17](#b-01770), Theorem [9.33](#b-01889)). The sector parts of $S^{(1)}(P_b)$ are
\int\big(\partial_b(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}),A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}\big),\qquad -\int(\partial_b\lambda,\lambda^*),\qquad \int\big(\partial_b(A|_V),A^*|_V\big)-\int(\partial_bc,c^*);

their sum is $S^{(1)}(P_b)$, and each sector part of $S^{(1)}(\Delta)$ of Section 10.8 is $2\int x^\mu$ times the density of the sector part of $S^{(1)}(P_{e_\mu})$ of the same sector, summed over $\mu$, plus a translation-invariant functional, with $e_\mu$ an orthonormal basis of $V$ and $x^\mu$ the coordinates.
Lemma 11.2 (Structure of the composite kernels).
• (i) The composite kernel along $x$ is $2\big(P\star\,v_x.\,P\star\otimes1\big)K_0=(v_x.\otimes1-1\otimes v_x.)$ applied to the square kernel.

• (ii) $(v_x.\otimes1+1\otimes v_x.)$ applied to the square kernel is $-4\big(\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon+T\partial_T\big)$ of the square kernel for $x=\Delta$ and $0$ for $x=P_b$. Hence the composite kernel along $\Delta$ is $2(v.\otimes1)$ of the square kernel plus $4(\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon+T\partial_T)$ of it, and the composite kernel along $P_b$ is $2(\partial_b\otimes1)$ of the square kernel.

• (iii) The square kernel and the composite kernels have components in $c\otimes A|_V$ and $A|_V\otimes c$ alone: as operators, $(P\star)^2$ and $P\star\,v_x.\,P\star$ map the slot of $A^*|_V$ to the slot of $c$ and the slot of $c^*$ to the slot of $A|_V$, and vanish on the other slots.

• (iv) In a graph the composite kernel is the vertex $S^{(1)}(x)$ with both legs on edges $P$. Its term $\int(v_x.A|_V,A^*|_V)$ contributes, with the leg $A|_V$ on the component $A\otimes A$ of $P$ and the leg $A^*|_V$ on the component $A^*|_V\otimes c$. Along $\Delta$ this internal vertex is
\int\big((2E+2)A|_V,A^*|_V\big)=2\int x^\mu\big(\partial_\mu(A|_V),A^*|_V\big)+2\int\big(A|_V,A^*|_V\big),

along $P_b$ it is $\int(\partial_b(A|_V),A^*|_V)$. The components of $P$ lie in $A\otimes A$, $\lambda\otimes\lambda$, $c\otimes A^*|_V$ and $A^*|_V\otimes c$ (Proposition [3.11](#b-00430)), so the terms of $S^{(1)}(x)$ in the sectors of $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$ and $c$, whose antifield legs are $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$, enter a cycle through the special edge.
• (v) $(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)$ annihilates the composite kernel; the operator $\partial$ of the composite kernel is odd and anticommutes with $Q$.

• (vi) At $T=\infty$ the component of the square kernel is $(Q^{GF})^2$ on the slot of $A^*|_V$, which is $2d^*$ with values in the slot of $c$ (Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (ii)), times $(-,-)^{-1}$ and
\int_\varepsilon^\infty\!\!\int_\varepsilon^\infty e^{-(s'+s'')|p|^2}\,ds'\,ds''=e^{-2\varepsilon|p|^2}|p|^{-4}:

a doubled edge with two Schwinger times $s',s''\in[\varepsilon,\infty)$, of momentum degree $-3$, which obeys the weight rule of Proposition [3.11](#b-00430) for the slots $c$ (weight $0$) and $A|_V$ (weight $1$).
Proof.

(i) The first equality is Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (i) along $\Delta$; along $P_b$ the same computation holds, $\partial_b$ preserving the pairing and commuting with $Q^{GF}$ and $H$ (Proposition [7.6](#b-01244)). For the second, $2P\star\,v_x.\,P\star=v_x.(P\star)^2+(P\star)^2v_x.$, along $\Delta$ because $[v.,P\star]$ is $Q^{GF}$ times a function of $H$ and commutes with $P\star$ (proof of Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (i)), along $P_b$ because $\partial_b$ commutes with $P\star$. For the even operator $X=(P\star)^2$, $(X\,v_x.\otimes1)K_0=(X\otimes1)(v_x.\otimes1)K_0=-(1\otimes v_x.)(X\otimes1)K_0$ by Lemma [9.15](#b-01755), $v_x.$ being even and pairing preserving.

(ii) Since $(v_x.\otimes1+1\otimes v_x.)K_0=0$, the left side is $([v_x.,X]\otimes1)K_0$. Along $\Delta$, $X=(Q^{GF})^2g(H)^2$ with $g(H)=\int_\varepsilon^Te^{-tH}dt$, $[v.,Q^{GF}]=-4Q^{GF}$ and $[v.,f(H)]=-4Hf'(H)$ (Proposition [7.10](#b-01286)). From $Hg'(H)=Te^{-TH}-\varepsilon e^{-\varepsilon H}-g=(\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon+T\partial_T)g-g$,
[v.,X]=-8X-4(Q^{GF})^2H\partial_H\big(g^2\big)=-8X-4\big((\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon+T\partial_T)X-2X\big)=-4\big(\varepsilon\partial_\varepsilon+T\partial_T\big)X .
Along $P_b$, $[\partial_b,X]=0$. Insert into (i).

(iii) $(Q^{GF})^2$ vanishes on the slots of $c$, $A$, $\lambda$, $\lambda^*$; on $A^*$ and $c^*$ it is $2d^*(A^*|_V)$ in the slot of $c$ and $-2dc^*$ in the slot of $A|_V$ (Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (ii)); $v_x.$ preserves the slots, and the components $A^*\otimes A$ and $c^*\otimes c$ of $K_0$ go to $c\otimes A|_V$ and $A|_V\otimes c$.

(iv) Applied to $A^*\otimes A$, the kernel $(P\star\,v_x.\,P\star\otimes1)K_0$ is the component $A^*\to A$ of $Q^{GF}$, then $v_x.$ on the slot of $A$, then the component $A\to c$ of $Q^{GF}$: the vertex $\int(v_x.A|_V,A^*|_V)$ between an $A\otimes A$ and an $A^*|_V\otimes c$ component, the factor $2$ counting the two orientations. On $A|_V$, $L_{2E}A|_V=2x^\mu\partial_\mu(A|_V)+2A|_V$ (Definition [7.4](#b-01226)).

(v) Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (iii) along $\Delta$; along $P_b$, $QP\star+P\star Q=e^{-\varepsilon H}-e^{-TH}$ commutes with $\partial_b$, which commutes with $Q$, so $Q(P\star\,\partial_b\,P\star)=(P\star\,\partial_b\,P\star)Q$. The identity $[\partial_\phi,Q]=\partial_{(Q\otimes1+1\otimes Q)\phi}$ of Lemma [9.15](#b-01755) gives the anticommutation; the composite kernel has degree $-1$.
(vi) Proposition [9.18](#b-01772) (iv) and $\big(\int_\varepsilon^\infty e^{-s|p|^2}ds\big)^2=e^{-2\varepsilon|p|^2}|p|^{-4}$. ∎
Definition 11.3 (Composite graphs and the arity-one counterterm of an operator).

Let $M$ be a local functional, $\delta$ a square-zero parameter of degree $-|M|$, $x\in\{\Delta,P_b\}$ and $P=P(\varepsilon,\infty)$. The composite graphs of $M$ along $x$ are the $\delta$-linear part of
\tfrac\hbar2\,\partial_{\text{composite kernel along }x}\,W(P,I+\delta M)_{\rm tree}:

the composite kernel closes two legs of a tree of vertices $I$ and one vertex $M$. The cycle so formed either passes through two letters $X_a$, $X_b$ of $M$, a composite cycle through the pair $(X_a,X_b)$ with trees of $I$ on its outputs, or passes through vertices of $I$ alone and is joined to $M$ by a tree through one letter, a composite loop of $I$ on a leg of $M$. The arity-one counterterm of $M$ along $x$ is $\hbar\,\mathrm{Sing}_\varepsilon$ of the amputated composite cycles through the pairs, summed over the pairs with the Koszul signs of [(10.4)](#b-01947). The singular part of the composite loops of $I$ is $I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]^{(1)}(x)$ (Proposition [9.24](#b-01822) (i)); its quadratic part along $\Delta$ is the unit times $\log\varepsilon$ times $Q\big(\int(\iota_xA|_V,c^*)-\tfrac12\int(\rho(x)\lambda^*,\lambda^*)\big)$, with no term in $\varepsilon^{-1}$ (Theorem [9.25](#b-01828) (i)).
Proposition 11.4 (The image of the composite graphs under $Q$).
For every local functional $M$, $x\in\{\Delta,P_b\}$ and $\varepsilon>0$, at $T=\infty$,

Q\big(\text{composite graphs of }M\text{ along }x\big)=-\tfrac\hbar2\,\partial_{\text{composite kernel along }x}\Big[\text{tree-level flow, }\delta\text{-linear, with one vertex }sM\text{ or one special edge}\Big],

the special edge joining a vertex $I$ to a letter of $M$, from $\{I,M\}_\varepsilon-\{I,M\}$, or two vertices $I$, from $\tfrac12(\{I,I\}_\varepsilon-\{I,I\})$. Since $\Delta_\varepsilon-\Delta_0=-\partial_{K_\varepsilon-K_0}$ (Definition [1.6](#b-00095), Proposition [4.27](#b-00837)), $\{f,g\}_\varepsilon-\{f,g\}$ is minus $f$ and $g$ joined by one edge $K_\varepsilon-K_0$; for $sM=0$ the right side is $\tfrac\hbar2\,\partial_{\text{composite kernel along }x}$ of the trees with exactly one edge $K_\varepsilon-K_0$.
Proof.

By Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (v), $Q$ anticommutes with $\partial$ of the composite kernel. By Proposition [4.26](#b-00828) at order $\hbar^0$, $Q\,W(P,J)_{\rm tree}$ is the tree-level flow of $QJ+\tfrac12\{J,J\}_\varepsilon$; the term $\hbar\Delta_\varepsilon J$ is of order $\hbar$, and its composite closure has two cycles. For $J=I+\delta M$ the classical master equation $QI+\tfrac12\{I,I\}=0$ (Proposition [1.14](#b-00173)) leaves $\tfrac12(\{I,I\}_\varepsilon-\{I,I\})$ in the $\delta$-independent part and $sM+(\{I,M\}_\varepsilon-\{I,M\})$ in the $\delta$-linear part. ∎
Definition 11.5 (Special-edge composite cycles and the composite pair kernel).
For two letters $X_a$, $X_b$ of any slots and $x\in\{\Delta,P_b\}$, the special-edge composite cycles of $(X_a,X_b)$ along $x$ are
\tfrac\hbar2\,\partial_{\text{composite kernel along }x}\,\partial_{K_\varepsilon-K_0}\big(\text{amputated chains from }X_a\text{ to }X_b\big):

the chains of Definition [10.10](#b-01992) with $k\ge1$ vertices of $I$ in which one edge $e_c$ is the composite kernel along $x$, one other edge $e_\sigma$ is the special edge, with the components of $K_0$ (each field slot with its antifield slot), which may end at a letter of any slot, and every remaining edge is $P(\varepsilon,\infty)$. By Proposition [11.4](#b-02329) they are minus $\tfrac\hbar2\,\partial$ of the composite kernel applied to the chains with one bracket-defect vertex. A chain is read with the signs of Lemma [10.5](#b-01957) along the chain from $X_a$, times
(-1)^{n(<\sigma)+n(<c)+[c<\sigma]},

where $n(<j)$ is the number of odd outputs at the vertices before the edge $e_j$, and $[c<\sigma]$ is $1$ if $e_c$ precedes $e_\sigma$ and $0$ otherwise; the outputs are left open as in Definition [10.3](#b-01936). The composite pair kernel of $(X_a,X_b)$ along $x$ is the coefficient of $\varepsilon^0$ of its special-edge composite cycles.

By Proposition [11.4](#b-02329), for $sM=0$ the image under $Q$ of the composite cycles through the pairs and of the composite loops on the legs is the sum of the special-edge composite cycles with trees of $I$ on their outputs, together with the composite closures in which the special edge lies on a tree; Theorem [11.14](#b-02397) identifies the composite term of a cocycle with the sum over its pairs of letters of the composite pair kernels.
Proposition 11.6 (Reachability and census).

• (i) The composite kernel joins a slot $c$ to a slot $A|_V$. The letters $c$ and $A|_V$ reach it directly; the letters $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$ and $A^*|_V$ reach it through one vertex, $A|_V(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})^2$ entered at $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda|_{S_+\otimes W}\lambda|_{S_-\otimes W^*}A|_V$ entered at $\lambda$, $([A|_V,c],A^*|_V)$ entered at $c$, each left at $A|_V$; the letters $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$, on which $P$ and the composite kernel have no component, reach it through the special edge, to a slot $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda$, $c$.

• (ii) A chain of Definition [11.5](#b-02335) exists for $45$ of the $55$ unordered pairs of the ten slots; the other ten are the pairs of two letters among $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*|_{S_+\otimes W^*}$, $\lambda^*|_{S_-\otimes W}$, $c^*$, which would need two special edges. Every chain conserves the degree, the fermion parity and the centre $\mathbb Z/4$ of $SL(4,\mathbb C)$, and its outputs carry the pair degree; the composite kernel has degree $-1$ and the special edge $+1$.

• (iii) Every chain has $k\ge1$ vertices. A chain with $k=1$ has the composite kernel at one letter and the special edge at the other, so $k=1$ occurs exactly for the pairs with a letter $A|_V$ and for the pairs $(c,A^*|_V)$, $(c,A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$, $(c,\lambda^*)$, $(c,c^*)$; the other pairs, the field pairs $(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$, $(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\lambda)$, $(\lambda,\lambda)$ among them, start at $k=2$.

• (iv) At the pair weight without derivatives the leg sets of the ten pairs of field letters are those of Table [11.1](#b-02349); the numbers of leg sets with $n\le3$ derivatives on the two letters, for the $21$ pairs of the active slots of Lemma [10.9](#b-01987), are those of Table [11.2](#b-02351).
Proof.

(i) Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (iii), Lemma [10.9](#b-01987) and the vertices of Definition [1.13](#b-00162). (ii), (iv) Enumeration of the chains with one composite kernel and one special edge, the vertices of $I$ and the components of $P$ and $K_0$, up to six vertices and output weight four above the pair weight; every chain is checked for degree, parity and the centre. A pair of two letters among $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$, $c^*$ needs an edge with a component on each letter; $K_0$ alone has one, and a chain has one special edge. (iii) A chain with $k=0$ would join the two letters by the composite kernel and the special edge at once; the rest is read off from the enumeration. ∎

Proposition 11.7 (Output bound).

• (i) A chain of Definition [11.5](#b-02335) with outputs of total Weyl weight $w$ has superficial degree $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-w$ before the insertion factor of $S^{(1)}(x)$; the factor $\partial_b$ adds one, and the translation-invariant part along $\Delta$ adds none.

• (ii) The composite pair kernel along $P_b$ is a translation-invariant local functional of Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}+1$; the composite pair kernel along $\Delta$ is local of Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$, the position counted at weight $-1$, at most linear in the position. Both have the pair degree and the parity $|X_a|+|X_b|$.

• (iii) Chains with $w\le w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}+1$ contribute to the kernel along $P_b$ and to the part along $\Delta$ linear in the position, chains with $w\le w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$ to the translation-invariant part along $\Delta$; a chain above these bounds has a vanishing limit as $\varepsilon\to0$.

• (iv) The number of output fields is at most $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}+1$ plus the pair degree for both kernels; the coefficients of $\varepsilon^{-m}$ of the special-edge composite cycles have Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}-2m$ along $\Delta$ and $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}+1-2m$ along $P_b$.

The same bounds hold for the composite cycles through the pair and for the arity-one counterterm, of degree one less than the pair degree: the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ of the arity-one counterterm of $X_aX_b$ has Weyl weight $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}$ along $\Delta$ and $w_{X_a}+w_{X_b}+1$ along $P_b$.
Proof.

(i) Every edge obeys the weight rule $w_1+w_2-4$: $P$ (Proposition [3.11](#b-00430)), $K_0$ (a field and its antifield have the weights $w$ and $4-w$, momentum degree $0$) and the composite kernel (Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (vi)); the count of Lemma [10.11](#b-01994) applies. (ii) The coefficient of $\varepsilon^0$ is a polynomial in the output momenta of degree equal to the superficial degree (Theorem [11.11](#b-02375)); along $\Delta$ the position enters once, through the factor $2x^\mu$ of Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (iv). Degree and parity: Proposition [11.6](#b-02342) (ii). (iii) A polynomial of negative degree vanishes, and so does the limit of a chain of negative degree with a special edge (Theorem [11.11](#b-02375)). (iv) Weyl weight plus degree is at least $1$ for every output (Proposition [10.12](#b-01998)), so the number of outputs is at most $w$ plus the pair degree. The statements on the arity-one counterterm follow in the same way from Lemma [4.6](#b-00594). ∎
11.2 Closed forms and locality
Definition 11.8 (Position part and translation-invariant part).

A local functional is in canonical form if it is written $\int\omega\,D$ with $\omega\in\Omega^4_c(\mathbb R^4)$ and $D$ a polynomial in letters, every derivative on a field. A map $M$ of local functionals, linear in $\omega$, of the form
M\Big(\int\omega\,D\Big)=\int\omega\,\big(x^\mu M_\mu(D)+M_0(D)\big),

with $M_\mu$, $M_0$ maps of densities at one point and $x^\mu$ the coordinates of $V$ in an orthonormal basis, has the position part $b^\mu M_\mu$ along $b\in V$ and the translation-invariant part $M_0$. A local functional $G=\int\big(x^\mu g_\mu+g_0\big)$ at most linear in the position has the position part $\int b^\mu g_\mu$ along $b$ and the translation-invariant part $\int g_0$. On plane waves, with the momenta of the fields independent and $\omega$ absorbing the total momentum, a graph is $\alpha\,\delta(\cdot)+\beta^\mu\partial_\mu\delta(\cdot)$, and $M_0$ corresponds to $\alpha$, $M_\mu$ to $i\beta^\mu$.
Lemma 11.9 (Translations and the canonical form).

$M$ is well defined, independently of integrations by parts against $\omega$, exactly when every $M_\mu$ commutes with the derivatives and $[M_0,\partial_\mu]=M_\mu$. Then $[M,\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}]$ is the map $\int\omega\,D\mapsto\int\omega\,b^\mu M_\mu(D)$. For $M=v.=\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ the position part is $2\partial_b$ and the translation-invariant part is the multiplication by $2w_D$; $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ has position part $0$.
Proof.

$M(\int\omega\,\partial_\mu D)$ and $M(-\int(\partial_\mu\omega)D)=\int\omega\big(M_\mu(D)+x^\nu\partial_\mu M_\nu(D)+\partial_\mu M_0(D)\big)$ agree for all $\omega$ exactly under the two conditions. Then $M(\int\omega\,\partial_bD)-\{S^{(1)}(P_b),M(\int\omega\,D)\}=\int\omega\,\big(M_0(\partial_bD)-\partial_bM_0(D)\big)=\int\omega\,b^\mu M_\mu(D)$, since $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ acts by $\partial_b$ on the fields and leaves the position and $\omega$ untouched. Lemma [9.16](#b-01761) (i) gives $v.\int\omega\,D=\int\omega\,2(x\cdot\partial+w_D)D$. ∎
Proposition 11.10 (Position decomposition).

• (i) For every pair of letters, the position part along $b$ of the composite pair kernel along $\Delta$ is twice the composite pair kernel along $P_b$. For every local functional the position part of its arity-one counterterm along $\Delta$ is twice its arity-one counterterm along $P_b$; on cocycles the position part of the composite term along $\Delta$ is twice the composite term along $P_b$; and the position part of $I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]^{(1)}(\Delta)$ along $b$ is $2I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]^{(1)}(P_b)$. In particular the quadratic part of the coefficient of $\log\varepsilon$ in $I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]^{(1)}(P_b)$ is $\tfrac12$ unit times $Q\big(\int(\iota_bA|_V,c^*)-\tfrac12\int(\rho(b)\lambda^*,\lambda^*)\big)$, and the quadratic part of the arity-one obstruction along $P_b$ vanishes.

• (ii) The translation-invariant part of the composite pair kernel along $\Delta$ is computed with the internal vertex $\int\big(2(x-x_O)^\mu\partial_\mu(A|_V)+2A|_V,A^*|_V\big)$, $x_O$ the point of the density, and pair by pair its commutator with $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ is twice the composite pair kernel along $P_b$.
Proof.

(i) By Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (iv) the internal vertex along $\Delta$ is $2\int x^\mu s_\mu+\int s_0$, with $\int s_\mu$ the internal vertex along $P_{e_\mu}$ and $s_0=2(A|_V,A^*|_V)$; insert $x^\mu=x_O^\mu+(x-x_O)^\mu$. On plane waves the factor $x^\mu$ is $-i\partial/\partial r^\mu$ of $e^{i(r,x)}$, with the momentum $r$ injected at the internal vertex and absorbed by $\omega$; its action on the momentum delta function is the position part, $-i$ times the graph with $\int s_\mu$ at $r=0$, which is $2\cdot(-i)$ times the graph along $P_{e_\mu}$; its action on the integrand is translation invariant. The same holds graph by graph for the composite cycles, their singular parts, the counterterm trees and the composite loops of $I$. Theorem [9.25](#b-01828) (i) gives the quadratic part along $\Delta$, which is $Q$ of $\int x^\mu$ times a density with $Q$ mapping letters to letters; Theorem [9.25](#b-01828) (ii) gives a quadratic obstruction along $\Delta$ without explicit position. (ii) The first statement is the decomposition of (i); the second is Lemma [11.9](#b-02366) applied to the composite pair kernel along $\Delta$, whose position part is given by (i). ∎

• (iv) The composite term of $O$ along $\Delta$ (Definition [10.36](#b-02186)) and along $P_b$ (Proposition [10.42](#b-02239)) is

a local two-body functional with no one-body term.

• (v) Hence the composite terms of the pairs and of the legs of Theorem [10.38](#b-02198), summed, equal the sum over the pairs of the composite pair kernels along $\Delta$: the nonlocal parts of the brackets of the letters $A|_V$, $\lambda$, $c$ with the renormalised composite two-point functional, $\log|p|^2$ of the leg momentum and $(p,a)(p,b)|p|^{-2}$ on $A|_V$ (Remark [9.26](#b-01842)), cancel against those of the images under $Q$ of the renormalised composite cycles through the pairs containing these letters.

with $I^{CT,(1)}$ short for $I^{CT}_{\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)}[\varepsilon]^{(1)}(x)$, an odd vertex, and the special edges joining the counterterm vertex to a vertex $I$. (v) Definition [10.36](#b-02186) writes the same limit as the sum of the composite terms of the pairs and of the legs (proof of Theorem [10.38](#b-02198)), so the two sums agree on cocycles, and the right side is local. Theorem 11.22 (The position part of $D_1$ is exact).

Assume a one-loop quantisation through arity two along $\Delta$ and $P_b$, that is, [(8.6)](#b-01446) modulo $\hbar^2$ in its components of arity at most two along these generators, and local representatives through arity two along $(\Delta,P_b)$ on a space $\mathfrak F$ of local functionals stable under $\Lambda$, with $P_1$ translation covariant, $P_1(\int\omega\,D)=\int\omega\,P_1(D)$ for a map $P_1$ of densities commuting with the derivatives; this holds when $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(P_b)$ is translation invariant. the position part of $D_1$ is $s$-exact on cocycles, with the arity-two component of $O$ as primitive.

By Corollary [8.17](#b-01500) (ii), $[\Lambda^{(1)}(\Delta),\Lambda^{(1)}(P_b)]+\Lambda^{(1)}([\Delta,P_b])$ is a graded commutator of $\Lambda^{(0)}$ with an operator built from $\Lambda^{(2)}(\Delta,P_b)$. with $H_1$ built from $\hbar L_1^{(2)}(\Delta,P_b)$. Lemma 11.23 (Position part of a bracket).
For a local functional $G=\int(x^\mu g_\mu+g_0)$, the position part along $b$ of $\{G,-\}$ is $\{\int b^\mu g_\mu,-\}$.
Proof.

The bracket contracts a slot of $g_\mu$ at $y$ with a letter $\partial^\alpha\varphi$ of $D$ at $x$ through $K_0$, which gives $\partial^\alpha_x(x^\mu\cdots)$; the term with no derivative on $x^\mu$ is $x^\mu$ times the bracket with $\int g_\mu$, and the others carry no position. ∎
Corollary 11.24 (The composite term along $P_b$ and the translation component).
Under the hypotheses of Theorem [11.22](#b-02449) and of Definition [10.36](#b-02186), on every cocycle $O\in\mathfrak F$:
• (i) twice the composite term of $O$ along $P_b$ minus the bracket of $O$ with the position part along $b$ of $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ is $s$-exact; this position part is

11.4 The dilatation identities in kernel form

Corollary [10.44](#b-02252) assumes that on cohomology the composite term minus the bracket with the finite counterterm beyond the field-counting functional induces $-\tfrac13$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$. By Corollary [11.16](#b-02416) this is a statement about the composite pair kernels, which splits into a statement along $P_b$ and a statement about the translation-invariant part.
Lemma 11.25 (One-body terms).

For $\theta=\theta_\lambda=\theta_V$, $\kappa_V=\kappa_\lambda=0$ and the quadratic part of $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ of Definition [11.19](#b-02433), the translation-invariant part of $-\big\{\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)-4\,\text{units}\cdot(\text{field-counting functional}),X\big\}$ on a field letter $X=\partial^\alpha\varphi$ is $(c_\varphi-2\theta\,w_X)$ units times $X$, with $c_\varphi=\tfrac23$ for $A|_V$ and $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\tfrac13$ for $\lambda$ and $\tfrac43$ for $c$, and its position part along $b$ is $-2\theta$ units times $\partial_bX$. At $\theta=-\tfrac13$ the translation-invariant part is $\tfrac23(2+|\alpha|)$ units times $X$ for every field slot and for $c$.
Proof.

$\{\int(A,A^*),X\}=X$, $\{\int(\lambda^*,\lambda),\lambda\}=-\lambda$ and $\{\int(c^*,c),c\}=-c$ (Lemma [4.21](#b-00796)), and the bracket of the sector part with a letter of its sector is $v.X$, with translation-invariant part $2w_XX$ and position part $2\partial_bX$ (Lemma [11.9](#b-02366)). At $\theta=-\tfrac13$: $\tfrac23+\tfrac23(1+|\alpha|)$, $\tfrac13+\tfrac23(\tfrac32+|\alpha|)$ and $\tfrac43+\tfrac23|\alpha|$ are all $\tfrac23(2+|\alpha|)$. ∎
Definition 11.26 (The identities in kernel form).

Let $\mathfrak F$ be a family of gauge-invariant cocycles of field letters, stable under $\Lambda$, satisfying (ii) and (iii) of Definition [10.36](#b-02186). The letter count is the derivation that multiplies a monomial $\int\omega\,X_1\cdots X_n$ of letters $X_a=\partial^{\alpha_a}\varphi_a$, $\varphi_a\in\{A|_V,A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},\lambda\}$, by $\sum_a(2+|\alpha_a|)$; it is defined on canonical forms, and its commutator with $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ is $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$. The three identities on $\mathfrak F$ are:
• (a) the cubic part of [(9.10)](#b-01821) forces $\theta=\theta_\lambda=\theta_V$;

• (b) the sum over the pairs, with the Koszul signs of [(10.4)](#b-01947), of the composite pair kernels along $P_b$ induces $-\tfrac13$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ on the cohomology of $\mathfrak F$;
• (c) the sum over the pairs of the translation-invariant parts of the composite pair kernels along $\Delta$ induces $-\tfrac23$ units times the letter count on the cohomology of $\mathfrak F$.
Remark 11.27 (Dependences among the identities).

(1) By Proposition [11.10](#b-02370) (ii), pair by pair the commutator of the translation-invariant part of the composite pair kernel along $\Delta$ with $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ is twice the composite pair kernel along $P_b$, and the commutator of the letter count with $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$ is $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$; hence (c) on $\mathfrak F$ and on $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),\mathfrak F\}$ gives (b) along $b$, and the content of (b) beyond (c) lies in the directions $b$ with $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),\mathfrak F\}$ outside $\mathfrak F$. (2) Identity (a) follows from (b) on three families with letters of one sector each, under the hypotheses of Theorem [11.22](#b-02449) (Proposition [11.29](#b-02492)); the cubic arity-one equation is then a consistency condition. (3) Identities (b) and (c) are identities between graph sums at the regulator of Definition [8.3](#b-01429); the numbers $-\tfrac13$ and $-\tfrac23$ are finite parts of special-edge cycles, which depend on the cutoff shape (Remark [10.48](#b-02274) (d), Proposition [10.23](#b-02092)). The statement independent of the scheme is the spectrum of $D_1$ at the coefficients fixed by the arity-two equation (Remark [10.48](#b-02274)).
Theorem 11.28 (Consequences of the identities).
Assume (a), (b) and (c) of Definition [11.26](#b-02477) on $\mathfrak F$.

• (i) $D_1$ minus four times the map of Theorem [10.16](#b-02027) induces $-(\tfrac13+\theta)$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ on the cohomology of $\mathfrak F$: the assumption of Corollary [10.44](#b-02252), for the solution with sector coefficient $\theta$.

• (ii) Under the hypotheses of Theorem [11.22](#b-02449), and if $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),O\}$ is not exact for some cocycle $O\in\mathfrak F$, $\theta=-\tfrac13$, and $D_1$ induces four times the map of Theorem [10.16](#b-02027); its spectrum on $\mathfrak F$ in a fixed classical Weyl weight is twice that of the one-loop dilatation coefficients, $-8$ units times the eigenvalues of $\sum_lH_{l,l+1}$ of [B03c, (1.1)–(1.3)] on planar families (Corollary [10.35](#b-02178)).
• (iii) In the translation-covariant scheme $P_1\cong0$ on $\mathfrak F$; otherwise Corollary [11.24](#b-02461) (iv) applies.
Conversely, if $D_1$ minus four times the map induces $-(\tfrac13+\theta)$ units times $\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ for equal sector coefficients, then (b) and (c) hold on $\mathfrak F$.
Proof.

(i) By Corollary [11.16](#b-02416), $D_1$ minus four times the map is the sum of the composite pair kernels along $\Delta$ minus the bracket with $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)-4$ units times the field-counting functional. Its position part along $b$ is, by (b) and Lemma [11.25](#b-02473), $2\cdot(-\tfrac13)\partial_b-2\theta\,\partial_b=-2(\tfrac13+\theta)\partial_b$ units. Its translation-invariant part is, by (c) and Lemma [11.25](#b-02473), $-\tfrac23$ units times the letter count plus $\sum_a(c_{\varphi_a}-2\theta w_{X_a})$ units, which is $-2(\tfrac13+\theta)w_O$ units, by $\sum_a(c_{\varphi_a}+\tfrac23w_{X_a})=\tfrac23\sum_a(2+|\alpha_a|)$. Together they give $-(\tfrac13+\theta)(2x\cdot\partial+2w_O)$ units, which is $-(\tfrac13+\theta)$ units times $v.$ (Lemma [11.9](#b-02366)). (ii) By Theorem [11.22](#b-02449) the position part of $D_1$, which is $-2(\tfrac13+\theta)$ units times $\partial_b$ on cohomology, is exact, and $\partial_bO$ is not exact for that cocycle, so $\theta=-\tfrac13$; then Theorem [10.16](#b-02027) and Corollary [10.35](#b-02178). (iii) Corollary [11.24](#b-02461) (iii). The converse reverses the two computations of (i). ∎
Proposition 11.29 (The arity-two equation fixes each sector coefficient).

Assume the hypotheses of Theorem [11.22](#b-02449) and of Definition [10.36](#b-02186). Let $\mathfrak F_\perp$, $\mathfrak F_\lambda$, $\mathfrak F_V$ be families of gauge-invariant cocycles whose two-field parts have letters of the sector of $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, of $\lambda$ and of $A|_V$ alone, each containing a cocycle $O$ for which $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),O\}$ is not exact. If (b) holds on $\mathfrak F_\perp$, then $\theta=-\tfrac13$; if it holds on $\mathfrak F_\lambda$, then $\theta_\lambda=-\tfrac13$; if it holds on $\mathfrak F_V$, then $\theta_V=-\tfrac13$. In particular (b) on the three families gives $\theta=\theta_\lambda=\theta_V=-\tfrac13$, the equality asserted in (a), and the cubic part of [(9.10)](#b-01821) admits the solution $\theta-\theta_V=\theta_\lambda-\theta_V=0$.
Proof.

By Corollary [11.16](#b-02416), Proposition [11.10](#b-02370) (i) and Lemma [11.23](#b-02457), the position part of $D_1$ is twice the sum of the composite pair kernels along $P_b$ minus the bracket with the position part of $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$. On the two-field part $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(\Delta)$ acts through its quadratic part; the bracket of the sector part of the sector of $X$ has the position part $2\partial_bX$ and the other sector parts have bracket $0$ with $X$, and the $\kappa$-directions are $s$-exact (Proposition [11.21](#b-02443) (ii)). With (b), on the cohomology of the family of the sector with coefficient $\theta_\star\in\{\theta,\theta_\lambda,\theta_V\}$,

\big(\text{position part of }D_1\text{ along }b\big)\cong-\tfrac23\,\text{units}\cdot\partial_b-2\theta_\star\,\text{units}\cdot\partial_b=-2\big(\tfrac13+\theta_\star\big)\,\text{units}\cdot\partial_b .

The left side is $s$-exact on cocycles (Theorem [11.22](#b-02449)) and $\partial_bO$ is not exact, so $\theta_\star=-\tfrac13$. The last statement is Proposition [11.21](#b-02443) (iii); the existence of the quantisation is a hypothesis of Theorem [11.22](#b-02449). ∎
Corollary 11.30 (The dilatation component without the cubic equation).

Under the hypotheses of Proposition [11.29](#b-02492), if (b) holds on $\mathfrak F_\perp$, $\mathfrak F_\lambda$ and $\mathfrak F_V$, and (b) and (c) hold on $\mathfrak F$, then on the cohomology of $\mathfrak F$, $D_1$ induces four times the map of Theorem [10.16](#b-02027), with spectrum $-8$ units times the eigenvalues of $\sum_lH_{l,l+1}$ on planar families, and $P_1\cong0$ in the translation-covariant scheme.
Proof.
Proposition [11.29](#b-02492) gives $\theta=\theta_\lambda=\theta_V=-\tfrac13$, and Theorem [11.28](#b-02484) (i)–(iii) applies. ∎
Proposition 11.31 (The planar scalar sector).

On the part with the outputs $A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ of the planar scalar sector (Proposition [10.40](#b-02222)), (b) and (c) hold as identities modulo terms whose sum over the cyclically adjacent pairs of every trace vanishes: per adjacent pair the composite pair kernel along $\Delta$ is $\big[-\tfrac16v.(X_aX_b)-\tfrac23X_aX_b\big]$ units and along $P_b$ it is $-\tfrac16$ units times $\partial_b(X_aX_b)$, so that on $O=\operatorname{tr}(\iota_{w_1}A\cdots\iota_{w_L}A)$ the composite term along $\Delta$ is $-\big(\tfrac13v.+\tfrac23L\big)O$ units, the composite term along $P_b$ is $-\tfrac13$ units times $\partial_bO$, and the sum of the translation-invariant parts is $-\tfrac43L$ units, $-\tfrac23$ units times the letter count. On the bilinears these are exact identities (Example [11.18](#b-02426)).
Proof.

By Proposition [10.40](#b-02222) (i), (e), the composite term of an adjacent pair is $-v.(X_aX_b)$ units, and the bracket with the renormalised composite two-point functional on a letter is $(\tfrac53v.X-\tfrac23X)$ units (Remark [9.26](#b-01842)); by Theorem [11.14](#b-02397) (v) their sum is the sum of the composite pair kernels, and the one-body term distributed over the two adjacent pairs of each letter gives the density per pair. For $L$ letters without derivatives the letter count is $2L$ and the translation-invariant part of $v.$ is $2L$: $-\tfrac13\cdot2L-\tfrac23L=-\tfrac43L$. Along $P_b$: Theorem [9.33](#b-01889), $-2+\tfrac53=-\tfrac13$. ∎
11.5 The composite kernels on the families

Throughout this section $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(N)$ at leading order in $N$ and $O$ is a single trace, with the conventions of Section 10.7. The projection to cohomology on the two-field part is the evaluation on the free equations of motion, $|p|^2=0$ on the scalar legs, the Weyl equation on the gaugino legs and transverse on-shell gauge legs, which removes the $s$-exact terms $s(\text{antifield}\times\text{field})$; total derivatives are kept, as descendants through $\omega$. The letters are written in the components of Definition [8.1](#b-01405).
Definition 11.32 (Test families).

Let $n_m:=\sigma^m_{1\dot1}=(0,0,1,i)$, a null vector, and $D_n:=n_m(\partial_m+[A_m,-])$, the covariant derivative $\iota_nd_{A|_V}$ along $n$; let $Z=\iota_wA$ with $w\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp\otimes\mathbb C$, $(w,w)=0$; let $\psi:=\lambda_1{}^i$ for a fixed $i$, the component $\alpha=1$ of $\lambda|_{S_+\otimes W}$; and let $F_{11}$ be the component $\alpha=\beta=1$ of $(\sigma^m\bar\sigma^n)_\alpha{}^\gamma\varepsilon_{\gamma\beta}F_{mn}$, $F_{mn}=\partial_mA_n-\partial_nA_m+[A_m,A_n]$, whose two-field part is a component of $dA|_V$ and whose three-field part is a component of $[A|_V\wedge A|_V]$. The test families are the spans of the following single traces and their gauge completions:
• the scalars: $\operatorname{tr}(\iota_{w_1}A\cdots\iota_{w_L}A)$, the bilinears, and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ sector of Proposition [10.32](#b-02160) for $L\le8$;
• twist two: $\operatorname{tr}\big(D_n^kZ\,D_n^{S'-k}Z\big)$, $0\le k\le S'$ (Proposition [10.34](#b-02171));
• the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ sector: single traces of the letters $Z$ and $\psi$ of Proposition [10.33](#b-02165), $L\le6$;
• the fermion $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sector: $\operatorname{tr}\big(D_n^k\psi\,D_n^{S'-k}\psi\big)$;

• two gaugino components: $\operatorname{tr}\big(D_n^k\psi^{(3)}\,D_n^{S'-k}\psi^{(4)}\big)$ with $\psi^{(3)}=\lambda_1{}^3$, $\psi^{(4)}=\lambda_1{}^4$, together with $\operatorname{tr}\big(D_n^kZ'\,D_n^{S'-k}F_{11}\big)$, $Z'$ the scalar letter with the R-symmetry weights of $\psi^{(3)}\psi^{(4)}$, with which the family closes;

Remark 11.36 (Method of computation).

Each special-edge composite cycle is evaluated exactly: the Gaussian loop integral and the integrals of [(11.1)](#b-02377) over the ordered subsimplices of the region where $\alpha_\sigma$ is the smallest coordinate, the letter derivatives through Proposition [11.12](#b-02381), the position through the injected momentum $r$ (Proposition [11.10](#b-02370)), the chains with $k=1$ through Proposition [11.13](#b-02389), the fibre algebra in explicit realisations of $V_{10}$ and $\Sigma$ over $\mathbb Q(i)$, and the colour words by Lemma [10.8](#b-01973), with its planar adjacent rule also checked in realisations of $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\mathfrak{gl}(3)$. In this evaluation the factor $(-1)^{[c<\sigma]}$ of Definition [11.5](#b-02335) is part of the chain convention when the special edge ends at $X_b$ and is applied as the factor $-1$ when the special edge joins two vertices of $I$. A second evaluation works in momentum space with the kernel form of Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (ii), $v.$ acting on the Fourier components as an Euler operator plus constants, Feynman parameters for the edges $P$ and the special Schwinger time integrated last, and applies the sign of Definition [11.5](#b-02335) as written. The two evaluations give the same off-shell entries with at most two outputs and no letter derivatives, for the pairs of bosonic letters and for the pairs with a gaugino letter or output, whose values lie in $\mathbb Q+\mathbb Q\log2+\mathbb Q\log3$ for $k\le2$, and the same family matrices on the scalars, on twist two for $S'\le4$, on the $\mathfrak{su}(1|1)$ sector, on the fermion $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sector for $S'\le5$ and on the gluon $\mathfrak{sl}(2)$ sector for $S'\le2$; the first evaluation extends twist two to $S'\le6$, and the second evaluation gives the two families with $F_{11}$ and a gaugino letter. A third evaluation, a Taylor expansion in momentum space at generic null leg momenta, gives the sums on twist two for $S'\le4$ along a generic $b$. Every integral is a four-dimensional Schwinger integral with the cutoff $\varepsilon$ on every edge.
11.6 The two-body kernels of $Q_1$, $S_1$ and $K_1$

For $x$ in a homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak{psl}(4|4)$, $\lambda_x$ is its $\mathrm{ad}_\Delta$ eigenvalue, $-1$ on $\Sigma$, $+1$ on $\Sigma^*$ and $+2$ for $K_b$, and the degree of $x$ in the position is $0$, $1$ and $2$ (Section 10.9). The two-body kernel of a pair of letters along $x$ is that of Proposition [10.45](#b-02258): the limit as $\varepsilon\to0$ of the local parts of the cycles through the pair with exactly one defect insertion, a special edge, the vertex $S^{(1)}(x)$ on the cycle, or the arity-one counterterm vertex of the operator. This section gives the lines that $S^{(1)}(x)$ forms on a cycle along $\Sigma$, $\Sigma^*$ and $K_b$, the output bounds, the relations of $S_1$ to $Q_1$ and of $K_1$ to $P_1$, the renormalisation freedom in the scheme of Sections 11.3–11.5, and the comparison of $Q_1$ with the one-loop differential of the holomorphic twist.
Lemma 11.37 (The lines along $\Sigma$, $\Sigma^*$ and $K_b$).

• (i) For $\xi\in\Sigma$ the quadratic part of $S^{(1)}(\xi)$ is $\int\mathrm{dvol}\big(-(\Gamma(\xi,\lambda),A^*)+\tfrac12(\rho(dA)\xi,\lambda^*)\big)$ (Proposition [7.11](#b-01303)). With both legs on edges $P$, its term $-\int(\Gamma(\xi,\lambda)|_V,A^*|_V)$ has the leg $\lambda$ on the component $\lambda\otimes\lambda$ of $P$ and the leg $A^*|_V$ on the component $A^*|_V\otimes c$: an odd line joining a slot $\lambda$ to a slot $c$, linear in $\xi$ and free of the position. The terms $-\int(\Gamma(\xi,\lambda)|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp},A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})$ and $\tfrac12\int(\rho(dA)\xi,\lambda^*)$, with a leg $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$ or $\lambda^*$, enter a cycle at the special edge.

• (ii) For $\eta\in\Sigma^*$, $S^{(1)}(\eta)$ is $S^{(1)}(\xi)$ with $\xi$ replaced by the value $\rho(x)\eta$ of the conformal Killing spinor, plus the translation-invariant term $-\int(\rho(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})\eta,\lambda^*)$ [(2.7)](#b-00314). Its line on a cycle is the line of (i) along $\rho(x)\eta$, linear in the position; the last term, with its leg $\lambda^*$, enters a cycle at the special edge.

• (iii) For $K_b$, with the vector field $v(x)=(x,x)b-2(b,x)x$, $S^{(1)}(K_b)$ forms on a cycle the composite line from $c$ to $A|_V$ with the kernel $P\star\,v.\,P\star=v.(P\star)^2+[P\star,v.]P\star$, quadratic in the position, at a finite endpoint $T$ (Definition [8.26](#b-01552) and the remark after Theorem [8.27](#b-01554)).
In each case every letter, $A^*|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp}$, $\lambda^*$ and $c^*$ included, is active (Lemma [10.46](#b-02264)).
Proof.

The components of $P$ are those of Proposition [3.11](#b-00430); $\Gamma(\xi,\lambda)\in V_{10}$ pairs with $A^*$ through its parts in $V$ and in $W_{\mathbb R}^\perp$. (ii) is [(2.7)](#b-00314), the first two terms being those of [(2.6)](#b-00312) at the spinor $\rho(x)\eta$. (iii) Definition [7.4](#b-01226) for the vector field of $K_b$ and Lemma [11.2](#b-02305) (iii), (iv) with this $v$. ∎

Proposition 11.39 (The special supercharges and the supercharges).
Let $\eta\in\Sigma^*$ and $b\in V$, so that $\rho(b)\eta\in\Sigma$.

• (i) Graph by graph, the position part along $b$ of the two-body kernel of $(X_a,X_b)$ along $\eta$ is the two-body kernel of $(X_a,X_b)$ along $\rho(b)\eta$; its translation-invariant part is computed with $S^{(1)}(\eta)$ at the spinor $\rho(x-x_O)\eta$, $x_O$ the point of the density, together with the term $-\int(\rho(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})\eta,\lambda^*)$.

• (ii) Under the hypotheses of Proposition [7.13](#b-01324) and Corollary [8.17](#b-01500), on cohomology, the position part along $b$ of $S_1$ along $\eta$ is $Q_1$ along $\rho(b)\eta$ minus the commutator of $\{S^{(1)}(\eta),-\}$ with $P_1$.

• (iii) On a family on which $P_1\cong0$, in particular on the families of Definition [11.32](#b-02508) in the translation-covariant scheme at $\theta=\theta_\lambda=\theta_V=-\tfrac13$, the position part of $S_1$ along $\eta$ is $Q_1$ along $\rho(b)\eta$ on cohomology, and $S_1$ along $\eta$ is fixed by $Q_1$ along $\Sigma$ up to the term of Proposition [7.13](#b-01324) linear in ${\not d}(\rho(x)\eta)=4\eta$. On the scalar bilinears this term is absent (Corollary [7.15](#b-01345)), and $S_1$ along $\eta$ is, on cohomology, the combination of the functionals of Corollary [7.15](#b-01345) with the coefficients of $Q_1$ along $\Sigma$ in Corollary [7.14](#b-01331).
Proof.

(i) By Lemma [11.37](#b-02549) (ii), $S^{(1)}(\eta)=\int x^\mu s_\mu+\int s_0$, where $\int s_\mu$ is $S^{(1)}$ along the constant spinor $\rho(e_\mu)\eta\in\Sigma$ and $s_0=-(\rho(A|_{W_{\mathbb R}^\perp})\eta,\lambda^*)$. Insert $x^\mu=x_O^\mu+(x-x_O)^\mu$ and argue as in the proof of Proposition [11.10](#b-02370) (i): on plane waves the factor $x^\mu$ is $-i\partial/\partial r^\mu$ of the momentum injected at the vertex, and its action on the momentum delta function is $-i$ times the graph with $\int s_\mu$; the same holds for the special edges, the vertices $S^{(1)}(\eta)$ on the cycle and the counterterm vertices, which are the defect insertions of Proposition [10.45](#b-02258). (ii) Corollary [8.17](#b-01500) (ii) at $(\eta,P_b)$: by Proposition [2.4](#b-00223), $[P_b,\eta]=\rho(b)\eta$, so $[\eta,P_b]=-\rho(b)\eta$, and $S^{(2)}(\eta,P_b)=0$ (Definition [2.15](#b-00332)). At order $\hbar$ the identity states that the commutator of $S_1$ along $\eta$ with $\{S^{(1)}(P_b),-\}$, plus the commutator of $\{S^{(1)}(\eta),-\}$ with $P_1$, minus $Q_1$ along $\rho(b)\eta$, is a graded commutator with $\Lambda^{(0)}$, which induces $0$ on cohomology; at order $\hbar^0$ the same identity is the statement of (i) for the classical transformation, which fixes the signs. By Proposition [10.47](#b-02268), $S_1$ along $\eta$ is at most linear in the position, and Lemma [11.9](#b-02366) identifies the first commutator with its position part. (iii) By Proposition [7.13](#b-01324) the representative of $S_1$ along $\eta$ at a point $x_0$ is a term linear in the value $\rho(x_0)\eta$ plus a term linear in $4\eta$; the first has the position part given by its value at $\rho(b)\eta$, and as $\eta$ and $b$ vary, $\rho(b)\eta$ spans $\Sigma$, so by (ii) it is the representative of $Q_1$ evaluated at $\rho(x_0)\eta$ on cohomology. ∎
Proposition 11.40 (Renormalisation freedom of the odd components and of $K_1$).

• (i) A field redefinition, a closed direction and the outer direction $G_B$ (Proposition [8.19](#b-01512) (a), (c)) change each component by minus the bracket with a local functional, a derivation of the letters: they change the one-body kernels and leave the two-body kernels unchanged. $G_B$ changes $Q_1$ along $S_+\otimes W$ by $-a$ and along $S_-\otimes W^*$ by $+a$ times the classical transformation, $S_1$ along $S_+\otimes W^*$ by $+a$ and along $S_-\otimes W$ by $-a$ times it, and leaves $K_1$ unchanged.

• (ii) The finite counterterms $\hbar F_1^{(0)}$ and $\hbar F_1^{(1)}(x)$ enter the one-body kernels (Remark [10.48](#b-02274) (a), (b)); the sector coefficients of Definition [11.19](#b-02433) enter the components along $\Delta$ and $P_b$.

• (iii) A finite part $\psi'$ of the operators changes the component along $x$ by $[\{S^{(1)}(x),-\},\psi']$ (Proposition [8.19](#b-01512) (b)). For $\psi'=\tfrac a2\{S^{(1)}(\Delta),-\}$ this is $\tfrac a2\lambda_x\{S^{(1)}(x),-\}$ (Proposition [9.34](#b-01895)): $+a$, $-\tfrac a2$, $+\tfrac a2$ times the classical transformation along $K_b$, $\Sigma$, $\Sigma^*$, a change of the one-body kernels. A finite part $\psi'$ that vanishes on $O$ changes the component of $O$ along $x$ by $-\psi'(\{S^{(1)}(x),O\})$; in this way the finite parts of the operators of the Weyl weight of $\{S^{(1)}(x),O\}$ enter the two-body kernels.

• (iv) The cutoff shape enters the finite parts of the special-edge cycles (Proposition [10.23](#b-02092), Lemma [10.24](#b-02098)), the composite pair kernels and the finite vertex [(10.6)](#b-02036).

• (v) In the translation-covariant scheme at $\theta=\theta_\lambda=\theta_V=-\tfrac13$, $P_1\cong0$ on the families of Definition [11.32](#b-02508) (Corollary [11.35](#b-02539)), and the condition $P_1=0$ of Definition [8.35](#b-01597) holds there with $\psi'=0$: the components along $K_b$, $\Sigma$ and $\Sigma^*$ are those of the scheme. For equal coefficients $\theta_P\ne\theta$ along $P_b$, the finite part with $a=(\theta-\theta_P)$ units gives $P_1\cong0$ and changes the components along $K_b$, $\Sigma$, $\Sigma^*$ by $a$, $-\tfrac a2$, $\tfrac a2$ times the classical transformation (Corollary [11.24](#b-02461) (iv)).
• (vi) The class $[Q^\xi_1]$ on the cohomology of $Q^\xi_0$, its kernel, image and rank are invariant under (i) and (iii) (Theorem [8.23](#b-01539)).

(i) Proposition [8.19](#b-01512); the bracket with a local functional is a derivation in its second argument, so it acts letter by letter. (ii) Remark [10.48](#b-02274) and Definition [8.16](#b-01496). (iii) Proposition [8.19](#b-01512) (b) and Proposition [9.34](#b-01895), with $[\{S^{(1)}(x),-\},\psi'](O)=\{S^{(1)}(x),\psi'(O)\}-\psi'(\{S^{(1)}(x),O\})$. (iv) Remark [10.48](#b-02274) (d). Proposition 11.42 (The chiral-primary bilinears along a rank-one supercharge).

Let $\xi\in S_+\otimes W$ be of rank one, $\xi_\alpha{}^i=u_\alpha z^i$, and let $w_1,w_2\in W_{\mathbb R}^\perp\otimes\mathbb C$ satisfy $\rho(w_1)\xi=\rho(w_2)\xi=0$. Then $(w_1,w_2)=0$, and under the hypotheses of Proposition [7.13](#b-01324) the component along $\xi$ of $O=\int\omega\,(\iota_{w_1}A,\iota_{w_2}A)$ vanishes at every order at which they hold: its classical part $\{S^{(1)}(\xi),O\}$ and $Q_1(O)$ are $0$, in every scheme in which the counterterms are equivariant for translations, $\mathfrak{so}(V)$, $\mathfrak{so}(W_{\mathbb R}^\perp)$ and $\mathfrak g$.
Proof.

$\rho(w_1)\rho(w_2)+\rho(w_2)\rho(w_1)=2(w_1,w_2)$ applied to $\xi\ne0$ gives $(w_1,w_2)=0$. By Corollary [7.14](#b-01331), for $(w_1,w_2)=0$ the component is a multiple of $\int\omega\,\big[(\iota_{w_1}A,(\rho(w_2)\xi,\lambda))+(\iota_{w_2}A,(\rho(w_1)\xi,\lambda))\big]$, which vanishes; the classical component is the same functional (proof of Corollary [7.14](#b-01331)). ∎
Remark 11.43 (The pair entries of the holomorphic twist).

The twisted one-loop differential is $\hbar Q^\xi_1(O)=\hbar L_1(O)^{(0)}+Q_1(O)-\tfrac12\hbar L_1(O)^{(2)}(\xi,\xi)-\cdots$ (Definition [8.22](#b-01535)), so its pair rule [BK, (3.7)–(3.8)] corresponds to the two-body kernels of $Q_1$ along $\xi$ and of the arity-two component along $(\xi,\xi)$.
